pages.title: Modular CyUI integration
pages.html:
Modular CyUI integration#

The standalone application uses CyUI 1.2.0, pinned to ff023e6.

Selected modules and replacements#

Core; DocumentViews (documents); Code; Images; Canvas; Diagnostics.

  • Free discussions use the common cached Markdown transcript with one state per thread. Closing a thread prunes its presentation cache.
  • The large picture viewer uses Images and its pointer navigation; decoding/texture ownership remains with the host.
  • Structured logs use Diagnostics, with a character-selectable text tab.
  • Core replaces the previous local monolith; no model/provider logic moves into the UI library.

Reproducible source and delivery#

app/cyui-source.json records every selected upstream file and its SHA-256. app/cyui.py and app/cyui_modules/*.py are unchanged official sources, normalized to LF. Do not edit them: host adapters live outside the library. Refresh only from the exact pinned checkout:

sh
python app/scripts/sync_cyui.py /path/to/CyUI

The sources are included with the application using its existing source-vendoring mechanism. Neither a developer checkout elsewhere on disk nor an editable pip installation is needed. There is one imgui-bundle renderer, at the version pinned in app/requirements.txt; no C++ umbrella, CMake demo/gallery, CEF, extra model, AI engine, NumPy installation or browser dependency is introduced by this migration. Existing application/DSP/rendering dependencies are kept where required.

Keep LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt with the product. The application's own license does not change. The Options licenses list identifies the upstream revision and source.

Host responsibilities and retained adaptations#

Character/world schemas, scene directives, voice annotations, streaming jobs, attachments, galleries and persistence remain host-owned. The roleplay scene retains its specialized editable directives, speech actions and media controls. DocumentViews is a documented Markdown subset, not a browser/Discord implementation. HTTP(S) links returned by it are handled by the host. No Web/CEF engine or unused Inspector is shipped.

SDK operations, permissions, exclusive groups, temporary AI task files, model installation, licenses/acceptance, generation recipes and Undo remain host-owned. No CyToolsCore runtime or AI library is copied into CyUI. English remains the default and French the persistent selectable second language.

Verification#

305 existing tests passed, one skipped; four new integration tests passed. Native Scene, Assistant, Assistant-Proposal, log and options views passed.

Run the adapter tests from app/ with the private Python:

sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_modular_ui.py -v

They verify pinned-source integrity, bounded log refresh/redaction and native ImGui frames across five themes, both densities, EN/FR and scale 1.0/1.5/2.0, plus the application-specific data/edit routing. This simulated DPI check is not a physical multi-monitor test. Windows native views are tested locally. Linux/macOS remain unverified by this migration; the source integration stays platform-independent.

Windows packages include the migrated sources and their license notices.

Final local results: 305 existing pytest tests passed and 1 skipped, plus 4 new adapter tests passed. Native checks passed for five EN views and nine FR view/subview combinations. A separate native fixture rendered the new picture surface and a Markdown conversation with bold, code and a table; capture: data/reports/cyui-native-picture-markdown.png.

CyUI license: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI/blob/main/LICENSE. The complete MIT text ships with the application, including when the upstream repository is private.

pages.title: Task files — SDK 0.9.0
pages.html:
SDK reference retained from the application sources. Its SDK version may differ from this application; the current operation reference is generated from CyTool.json.

Task files — SDK 0.9.0#

SDK sessions are temporary by default. A task can contain several jobs; completion of one producer must not delete results needed by consumers. Models, application code, shared installation caches and the original source files are never task artifacts.

Tool implementation (mandatory)#

Configure the accepted input root once in create_runtime, before starting:

python
runtime.configure_inputs(DATA / 'inputs', fields={    'image_to_mesh': ['image_file'],    'synthesize': ['references.*.audio'],})

Use the same root as the existing input resolver (including any configured environment variable). Declare every input-file field, including nested array fields. These fields accept absolute external paths; the SDK copies the source into a unique task-owned subdirectory of the accepted input root before calling the handler. Existing relative paths are also copied. A model path, LoRA, export destination or executable is NOT an input artifact: do not declare these in fields. Keep file format/size validation in the handler. The shared import bundle limit defaults to 8 GiB, configurable by the Tool. All generated files, intermediate files and worker diagnostics MUST use JobContext.path. Never write generated media into a global directory. Explicit user saves (profiles, model registration, installation) remain persistent operations.

AI / MCP use#

  • Call operations with an absolute input path directly; no shell copy is required.
  • Or call cy_import_file({"source":"D:/project/image.png"}). The Tool process copies it and returns path (absolute), relativePath, SHA256 and size. Supply path to the operation. OBJ/MTL/textures and GLTF/BIN references are copied automatically. Additional files can be passed as companions, relative paths from the source directory; directory structure is preserved. Import the bundle before submitting it. This never downloads a model.
  • Poll cy_get_job; read/consume the results while the task remains open.
  • To preserve a result, use cy_export_job({"jobId":"...","destination":"D:/project/results"}). This copies the job bundle, including supporting files, into a unique destination directory outside the runtime; returned output paths point to the exported copy.
  • Call cy_finish_task({}) after all consumers finish. It removes imported copies AND whole job workspaces: generated results, intermediates and logs. It never removes the original files or the explicit exported bundle. An active worker returns Busy; cancelRunning:true requests cancellation and defers deletion until workers stop.
  • Disconnect also finishes all connection-owned tasks. A forgotten idle task expires after 3600 seconds by default. cy_keep_task_alive renews it; active workers are never removed by expiration. cy_begin_task accepts retentionSeconds (1..86400). Its returned sessionId can be passed to operation envelopes and task controls for concurrent task graphs. Finish each Tool's task only after downstream consumers have imported or consumed its output. Paths between machines require a transfer transport; a local path refers to the Tool's host.

SDK equivalents: CreateSession, ImportFile, SubmitJob, ExportJob, FinishTask, KeepTaskAlive; same authenticated ownership in JSONL and HTTP. Native Python:

python
with runtime.task(actor) as session_id:    job = runtime.submit(actor, session_id, 'image_to_mesh', {'image_file': source})    result = runtime.wait(actor, job['jobId'], timeout=300)    saved = runtime.export_job(actor, job['jobId'], destination)

The context manager closes on exceptions as well. Normal runtime shutdown cleans remaining temporary tasks. On restart, recorded temporary tasks are recovered for cleanup; recorded live worker processes block deletion. A redirected workspace or a locked file produces cleanupError and retries, never an unsafe recursive deletion. Do not claim that an OS-denied source can be read: the MCP must return a useful error.

Standalone and compatibility#

Interactive UI sessions MUST explicitly use temporary=False; their generated results remain available after closing the UI. Imported working copies still disappear on session/runtime close. CLI invoke and saved-configuration replay remain persistent for backwards compatibility. AI automation should use task sessions via SDK/MCP. Pre-0.9 sessions have no temporary flag and are preserved; there is no destructive migration of old inputs/results. Small SQLite job/session history remains, with the parameters and output payload removed for purged jobs (artifactsDeleted:true). Model weights and secrets must not be put into a job workspace or export bundle.

Verification required before delivery#

Test external image/audio/video/mesh inputs without manually placing them under the Tool; assert the real resolver accepts the staged path. Test bundles, failed/cancelled jobs, disconnect, expiration, exports, client isolation and a worker still running. Verify every configured file field, not only one selected Tool. A transport test is not proof of a new full AI inference run; report the distinction explicitly.

These fields accept absolute external paths; the SDK copies the source into a unique task-owned subdirectory of the accepted input root before calling the handler. Tool delivery checklist#

Follow StandaloneDelivery, FullOperationAccess and TaskFiles before delivering a Tool.

  • Validate the manifest and execute its automated tests.
  • Launch the standalone from outside its installation folder; verify English/French, configuration persistence, copyable logs and every exposed business operation.
  • Exercise CLI and real MCP calls, including external inputs, result export, cancellation and task cleanup after workers stop.
  • Validate real model inference separately from synthetic transport tests.
  • Record the executed platform, model revision, output format and resource measurements.
  • Keep machine-specific reports under the Tool's data/reports directory.
  • State untested platforms and operations explicitly. A scaffold alone is not a delivery.

Unreal integration#

CyUEMCPSDK adapts CyToolsCore contracts to Unreal plugins. Follow its Docs/Integration.md and Docs/UpdateExistingPlugin.md. For an existing plugin, embed and adapt the C++ sources into its existing modules; the separate reference plugins are development examples, not mandatory dependencies. The Python companion uses CyToolsCore without copying its runtime or schemas.

Authentication, jobs, permissions and temporary task files retain the Core contract. Unreal assets integrated into a project remain persistent project changes. Provider transports are included in the SDK; CyAIConnectorLab is not a dependency. External MCP access and embedded assistant tool access require separate integration and validation. pages.title: Publishing the CyDoc reader
pages.html:
Publishing the CyDoc reader#

The web manual and the embedded manual are the same complete CyDoc HTML export. Markdown files remain editable sources; GitHub Pages serves the generated reader, including its navigation, full-text search, locales, styles, scripts and local media.

Regenerate and stage#

From the repository root, with Node.js 22+ and Python 3.11+:

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --install --checkpython app/tests/test_documentation.pypython app/tests/test_pages.pypython app/documentation/publish.py

The locked, vendored CyDoc package provides the generator. CI needs no access to the upstream private repository and installs no model or application engine. The publisher validates app/help and copies it byte-for-byte into _site, adding only .nojekyll and a staging marker. It never publishes application data/, runtime/, weights, credentials, conversations or generated user outputs. Do not hand-edit _site or app/help; edit the sources in sources.json instead. Source text hashes and indexed source copies use UTF-8 with LF newlines, and licence ordering is case-independent, so Windows and Linux produce the same reader. The original source documents are preserved.

Automatic deployment#

.github/workflows/documentation.yml rebuilds on pushes to main and can also be started manually from Actions. Only _site is uploaded to the github-pages artifact and deployed by the official Pages action. Set repository Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source to GitHub Actions.

The root English README links to #/en/overview, and the French README to #/fr/overview; the reader's language selector remains available on both. Page and section links use hash routes so they work beneath a project Pages URL and from an offline file:// URL without server rewrites.

Embedded help#

The full app/help remains in the application distribution. F1 and Options keep opening its local file URL. Publishing introduces no network dependency into embedded help and does not replace it with a web link.

Public reader: Documentation.

pages.title: Local documentation (CyDoc)
pages.html:
Local documentation (CyDoc)#

The editable Markdown listed in sources.json remains the source of truth. build.py imports it into CyDoc with stable page IDs, local media, full operation schemas and a lexical index of the shipped app/tool.py. Original French guides are retained; absent translations are explicit and tracked. Do not hand-edit app/help.

From the application root (Node.js >=22 and npm are build requirements only):

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --installpython app/documentation/build.py --checkpython app/help_docs.py --page overview --locale en

--install installs the locked generator under runtime/documentation-build, outside the shipped application. Subsequent builds need no installation. An already built CyDoc checkout/package may be selected with --cydoc-root PATH.

The complete generated app/help/ is shipped with application/update archives. Open app/help/index.html through a file URL. F1 opens contextual help; Options provides manual and workspace buttons. No HTTP server, CDN, network request or Node.js is needed for reading. External reference links remain optional external navigation.

CyDoc is pinned in cydoc-source.json and distributed under MIT; its full notice is in this directory, app/help and root LICENCES. Preserve generated third-party notices. MeshStudio alone includes an original procedural GLB with the mesh module and Three.js. Other modules are selected from actual imported media. Unused module scripts are absent. No interactive graph, GIF decoder or video player is added merely because an application can produce that format.

Review app/help/migration-report.json for old/missing links and translation-report.json for missing/stale translations. SDK reference pages are labelled separately from actual application capabilities. Linux/macOS launchers remain unverified unless a validation report records an execution on those platforms.

Web documentation#

Documentation · Français. See Publishing the reader for the GitHub Actions workflow and local staging commands. Embedded help continues to work offline.

pages.title: CyDoc migration validation
pages.html:
CyDoc migration validation#

Scope#

Existing user/developer guides, local illustrations, shipped operation schemas and the public Python entry-point source were migrated. The original Markdown is retained as editable source and for GitHub links. App/help is generated and includes all reader resources. Node.js is required only for regeneration; the reader uses local classic scripts and file URLs.

Checks executed on Windows#

  • Pinned CyDoc 0.1.0 built from revision 774f2a7eabf7dd181a98ffc5add115b580b67f42.
  • App-local npm lockfile installation and full CyDoc build/check.
  • Python routing tests: English/French, legacy paths, Unicode, spaces/hash characters, media links, unknown page fallback, browser failure, active operation and common anchors.
  • Native ImGui test-engine clicks on both help buttons and F1, using the product interpreter. The browser call was intercepted to assert its file URL without launching tabs.
  • The full standalone Options window was opened and closed in an isolated application copy.
  • Generated reader tested in a DOM fixture with network calls forbidden: rendering, operation links/anchors, language switch and in-window image expansion/Escape when used.
  • The pinned CyDoc core, interactions and packed-asset suites passed (25 tests), including keyboard/pointer controls and reading-position restoration.
  • Distribution selections are checked for the entire help tree and notices.

Limits#

The automation browser blocks file URLs. A real browser visual check of file-origin storage, layout, codecs and WebGL remains necessary; DOM fixtures do not prove it. Linux and macOS were not executed. Touch-device behavior is covered by library interaction fixtures, not a physical touch-device run. Existing missing translations remain visible in translation-report.json. No model inference was needed or rerun for this migration. The migration report records old missing references; SDK reference documents may describe older SDK releases and are explicitly labelled separately from current operation contracts.

Regenerate and verify#

From the application root:

sh
python app/documentation/build.py --installpython app/documentation/build.py --checkpython app/tests/test_documentation.pypython app/help_docs.py --page overview --locale en --print-url

Existing release builders regenerate/validate the manual before packaging. When a builder uses git archive, commit the generated reader together with its source changes first. Keep the complete app/help directory and LICENCES/CyDoc-MIT.txt in the delivered product.

pages.title: CyTools_PersonaRP — developer documentation
pages.html:
CyTools_PersonaRP — developer documentation#

Documentation · Français

cy.tool.personarp, built on CyToolsCore 0.10.1. Local roleplay with persistent characters, a shared world, relationships, and machine-readable scene descriptions for image and video tools. No model is part of the repository: engines and weights are downloaded from the interface (Models tab, Voice tab), each at a pinned revision and verified by SHA-256.

License: GPL-3.0-only (../LICENSE). It covers the code, the window, the ComfyUI node pack (which carries its own copy of the licence), the Colab project and the example worlds. The SDK, CyToolsCore 0.10.1, is MIT: ../LICENCES/CyToolsCore-MIT.txt and LICENSE-CyToolsCore.txt (the notice the 0.10.1 scaffold puts beside a Tool's code) hold its full text, and ../LICENCES/SOURCES.txt lists the sources of every component. LICENCES/ is in git, in the release zip (with Python-Runtime-Notices.txt written by build_release.py) and in the Colab project. Model weights are downloaded separately under their own licences (licenses.json, llm-catalog.json, tts-catalog.json).

Install, build, run#

text
py -3.11 -m venv runtime/pythoncd app && ../runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt

The requirement file installs CyToolsCore 0.10.1 (MIT) from its public repository, https://github.com/MrMybal/CyToolsCore, pinned to commit a8d200f2d0ba — the code this Tool was migrated to and verified against. git must be on the PATH: pip clones that commit. Going back to 0.1.1 means its commit and its requirement (CyToolsCore 0.9.0 at 442f53740fc6); release.json carries runtime_abi python311-cytools010-…, so the Updates tab refuses to put this application on a runtime that still has the 0.9 SDK, which would ignore the exclusion groups.

Task Command
Regenerate the manifest runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe app/build_manifest.py
Tests (no model) runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest app/tests -q
Real MCP session runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe app/tests/acceptance_mcp.py
Real speech acceptance runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe app/tests/acceptance_voice.py
Voices of the example characters (GPU, resumable) runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe app/build_example_voices.py [01-valdrenn ...]
Play two example worlds with the real model runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe app/tests/acceptance_examples.py
Real translation + voices per language runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe app/tests/acceptance_translation.py [llm-model]

Two environments#

runtime/python is the Tool's own light environment: the SDK, Dear ImGui, soundfile. The speech stack lives apart in runtime/engines/voice (PyTorch CUDA, Qwen3-TTS, Whisper, about 8 GB), built by app/setup_engine.py at its final path and never moved. Nothing heavy is imported by the window, the CLI or the MCP server: the workers in app/workers run inside the engine and talk over the JSON-lines protocol in personarp/workerhost.py.

The workers import personarp.voice.annotations and nothing else of ours, which is why the mark vocabulary sits in personarp/marks.py on the standard library alone — the SDK is not installed in the engine.

Speed, pitch and takes#

personarp/voice/prosody.py applies the sheet's voice.speed (0.25–4) and voice.pitch (±12 semitones) after the model, in numpy: WSOLA time-stretching by pitch-ratio/speed, then an FFT resampling to the target length, one pass each. _render_voice shapes every segment of a take and rebuilds the whole line and its timeline; _speak_batch shapes each line with its own speaker's settings; capture_voice_take neutralises both, so a stable voice is never cloned from a shaped take. Measured on a real 18 s take: durations exact, fundamental within 1 %, 0.05–0.2 s of processing.

personarp/takes.py: a line's audio record (turn, or translation) keeps its old shape for the chosen take and lists every take under takes. speak_turn writes a new file (turn-NNN-<lang>-<stamp>.wav) and chooses it; choose_take and remove_take (to audio/<session>/.trash) take the execution lock, since a generation rewrites the whole scene when it saves. A record from before takes existed counts as one take. A retranslated line sends the takes of its old words to the trash.

Microphone and dictation#

gui/recorder.py records from the chosen input (the default input's audio API only, so a device is listed once) at 24 kHz, or at the card's own rate when it refuses, into data/inputs/micro-<purpose>-<stamp>.wav; nothing is opened before a button is pressed. The Voice tab records a take (stops at 30 s) for create_stable_voice; the Scene tab's Dictate records up to 2 minutes and submits transcribe, whose text is appended to the message. No operation opens the microphone: from the CLI or MCP, transcribe takes a file.

Messages in the window's language#

Operations answer in English for every interface. locales/messages.json holds each message as the code writes it, variable parts as {0}, {1}…; personarp/messages.templates() reads them from the code (raises, returned reasons, reason +=, problems, notes), and tests/test_messages.py fails when one has no French. gui.state.shown() translates what the window shows — errors (the code stays visible in brackets), notices, progress steps, batch problems and line errors — matching the whole message and translating variable parts that are messages themselves (a reason followed by its consequence, a language name).

Jobs and the execution lock#

The manifest declares Concurrent (16 workers): the window waits for the answer of a list, a sheet or a session (AppState.call), and under Sequential those requests queued behind a voice being spoken — the window stopped drawing, Windows declared it hung, and closing it lost the voice already generated. Every job that uses the GPU or stops an engine (chat, speak*, translate, describe_image, installations, update, unload_model, release_voice, the take operations — 21 in all) takes personarp.locks.exclusive and is declared in the SDK's gpu exclusion group (CyToolsCore 0.10, operations[].exclusiveGroups): the runtime itself keeps the next ones Queued, in order, cancellable, without a worker slot. personarp/exclusion.py reads that list from tool.py (handlers and wrappers that take the lock) and build_manifest.py writes it, so the two cannot drift. The lock no longer queues anything: it keeps other processes out (the window and an MCP server have separate runtimes, which the groups do not coordinate) and lets a job that holds it take it again (the maintenance wrapper, then its handler). tests/test_concurrency.py checks that the grouped list equals what the code locks, that the installed SDK enforces groups, that a list is answered at once while a job holds the lock, that a second job stays Queued then runs, that a queued job can be cancelled, that unloading the model waits for the generation, and that another process gets Busy.

The binary release#

app/build_release.py builds the release from the commit HEAD (git archive; uncommitted changes are refused) into runtime/build/release/<version>/. In the portable zip, runtime/python is not a virtual environment but a private CPython 3.11, copied from an official installation without site-packages, byte-code, Tk, IDLE or the test suite. Its interpreter and the DLLs it loads live in runtime/python/Scripts, so every path the Tool already uses (the launcher, the manifest's executable, the ComfyUI nodes, the voice engine setup) finds it where a virtual environment would put it; Python finds Lib/ by searching upwards from the executable. runtime/python/pyvenv.cfg holds only include-system-site-packages = false: with no home line the interpreter keeps its own folder as prefix, and site (frozen into the 3.11 executable, so editing Lib/site.py would change nothing) turns the per-user site-packages off, so a user's own packages never shadow the Tool's. Packages are installed at the versions of the development runtime (constraints from its pip freeze), console-script wrappers (which hold the absolute path of the build machine) and every __pycache__ are removed, runtime/python/THIRD-PARTY.md lists each package and its licence, and runtime/build-info.json records the commit and the versions. The build fails if the packaged interpreter reads anything outside the package, or if any file of the package names the project folder, the base Python, the user profile (long or 8.3 form) or the machine name. The voice engine is created from this interpreter with venv, which the copy keeps.

app/tests/acceptance_release.py extracts the zip into a new folder with a space in its name and runs it with PATH reduced to Windows, no PYTHON* variable and a working directory outside the package: layout, interpreter isolation (including a module planted in a per-user site-packages, which must stay invisible while the machine's own CPython, the control, imports it), the CLI, a real MCP session whose client is granted filesystemExternal and imports an example world, the launcher opening two tabs, a venv made from the private interpreter, and with --tests the whole suite inside the copy.

Voice#

A capability is a set of weights, not a flag. Qwen3-TTS ships one variant per capability and refuses the others outright, so delivery.VARIANTS maps the mode to the weights and _model_for substitutes with an explanation rather than letting the model answer with a message about tokenizer types:

Mode Weights Used when
clone 1.7B-Base, 0.6B-Base a stable voice is attached — the normal case
design 1.7B-VoiceDesign the sheet carries a written voice description
custom 1.7B-CustomVoice, 0.6B-CustomVoice a preset speaker

A stable voice is a document in data/voices holding the reference recording, its exact transcript, its SHA-256 and the variant that reads it. It is locked on creation: changing the reference or the model is refused, because a voice that quietly changes is worse than no voice. verify_voice reports a moved or modified recording.

The take produced by capture_voice_take is copied to data/voices/takes before the job workspace disappears, so it can still be registered later.

spoken_text decides what reaches the worker: the scene directive never does, narration does only when the sheet says so, and annotations are kept only for a backend that understands them.

generate_voice_clone has no instruction input, so in clone mode the acting direction and the tone marks are built but not read by the model; only pauses (rendered as silence by the plan) reach a cloned voice. The sheet says so next to the stable voice picker.

Languages#

voice.language on the sheet is the character's own language and wins over the language recorded on the stable voice (delivery.native_language). voice.languages[] holds one entry per other language (LANGUAGE_VOICE_SCHEMA), and payload_for(..., language=) applies it:

source What speaks Mode
same, accent: keep (also: no entry) the main voice; the in-context clone carries the take's accent clone, full reference
same, accent: native the main voice's timbre only clone, x_vector_only
voice another stable voice, typically captured in that language clone
design a voice invented from the entry's description design
preset a preset speaker with the entry's direction custom

Without a stable voice, same asks for the accent in the instruction instead. A missing per-language voice falls back to the main voice with a note, never silently. The payload's voice_plan (returned as voicePlan) says what was really used.

Every translation request carries translation.context_block() — the world (genre, tone, summary, setting; places, factions and glossary terms, those the batch mentions first), who speaks and how (personality, speech style, register, vocabulary, accent, tics), the sheet's current state (situation, place, time, mood), the session title and the caller's context note — bounded to 3 000 characters, and translation.earlier_lines(): the four turns before the batch in their original words, with their translation when one exists or was just made. The system prompt says the context is for understanding only. A text given with a session_id is translated with that scene as context and nothing is stored; world_id gives a text without a character its world. Measured with tests/acceptance_translation_context.py.

The lexicon. world.term_translations[<Language>][<term>] = {text, source: model|person, model, at}. translation.world_terms() lists the glossary terms, locations and factions; mentioned_terms() finds them in a text (accent- and case-folded, whole words, a plural s/x allowed). Terms mentioned but not yet rendered go through one constrained pass (terms_messages, terms_schema — the meaning is a hint, a rendering is bounded to a name's length) and parse_terms keeps only plausible names (no sentence, a leading article lower-cased); they are recorded in the world unless keep_terms is off. Each batch then gets the renderings of the terms it uses as names (used_as_name: a compound always, a single word only where it is capitalised), missed_terms checks the answer (article dropped, plural and possessive allowed), a line that dropped one is asked again once with insist, and what is still missing is stored as termsMissed on the turn. save_world keeps the lexicon on disk (a window's older copy cannot wipe it); it changes through translate and set_term_translations only (source: person is never replaced), and translation_terms reads it. A first version of the terms prompt presented the meaning beside the term and a 4B model translated the meaning; tests/acceptance_translation_terms.py now fails on a description-like rendering.

translate (see personarp/translation.py) masks the delivery marks as ⟦n⟧ tokens, batches turns up to 2 400 characters, constrains the answer to one non-empty string per turn, restores the marks and reports any the model lost. Translations are stored beside the turn (turn.translations[<Language>] = {text, model, at, marksLost, audio?}); the original is never rewritten, already translated turns are skipped unless overwrite, and a changed translation drops the take made from the old words. speak_turn speaks a stored line in its own language or a translation and keeps the take under data/sessions/<persona>/audio/<session>/. create_stable_voice with for_language attaches a voice to that language only; capture_voice_take ignores the per-language entries so a take is always the voice described.

Batch tasks#

speak_batch (list inline: text as a script, CSV or JSON — format auto-detects — or items, or resume) and speak_batch_file (anything read from disk: file, personas, use_library; filesystemExternal) share one handler. The split exists because permissions are per operation: an AI client with no permission must be able to send its lines, while reading an arbitrary file stays reserved, like import_personas. list_batches lists data/batches. Tasks are ordinary jobs: several submitted in a row wait behind the runtime's Sequential policy, and the window queues them in App.pending.

A task's own characters. personas are bundles exported by export_personas with the recordings. batches.import_task_personas copies them into <task>/personnages/ (fiches/, mondes/, voix-stables/ with each recording and a relative path, import.json) and never into the library; within the task a taken identifier gets a new one and the sheets follow it. A voice without its recording, or whose recording does not match reference_sha256, is refused and listed in problems. batches.load_task reads them back — on every run, resume included — and checks each recording against its fingerprint again. delivery.payload_for takes these voices as voices=; _stable looks there before the library. Cast searches the task's sheets first, then the library unless use_library is off; the source of each speaker (task, library, voice) is recorded on the line so a resume speaks with the same one. library.voice_ids / _voice_documents export the per-language voices as well as the main one — before, an exported character lost its English voice.

Line ids. batches.assign_ids gives every line its own id (CSV id column, JSON id, script ID | Name: text) or its number; a repeated id (case-insensitive, as on Windows) is reported on the second line instead of overwriting the first take. file_stem names the take after the id (safe_name keeps SC01_L005 as it is, reserved device names are prefixed).

The handler (tool.py, _speak_batch) parses (personarp/batches.py), finds each speaker (identifier, name, alias, then a run of whole words only one name holds — an ambiguous name is an error, never a guess), builds each line's payload with delivery.payload_for exactly as speak does, and groups the lines by (mode, model): one worker request per set of weights. dry_run stops there and returns the plan; it imports the task's characters into the job's own workspace, makes no task folder, takes no lock and reserves no VRAM.

The worker (synthesize_batch in workers/tts_worker.py) loads the weights once, cuts every line into its plan, pools the passages of all lines longest first (personarp/voice/batching.py) and calls generate_voice_clone / generate_voice_design / generate_custom_voice with lists — Qwen3-TTS batches them in one forward pass, each with its own voice prompt, language and instruction. One clone prompt is encoded per reference, however many lines use it. batch_size 0 measures instead of guessing: a first batch of PROBE_BATCH (4) passages — the longest, so the dearest — gives the cost of one passage (max_memory_allocated above the weights), and fit sizes the next batches from the room left (SAFETY 0.85, 32 at most). The worker caps its allocator with set_per_process_memory_fraction at what was free when it started, minus 1.5 GiB: on Windows the driver otherwise spills into system memory instead of failing — a first version asked for 26 GB on a 24 GB card and ran 3.7 times slower than one line at a time. Under the cap an oversized batch raises out-of-memory, is halved and retried, and never grows again (generate_all). The cap is lifted after the batch so single takes are not limited. Measured on an RTX 3090, 16 cloned lines: size 1 76.5 s, 4 26.4 s, 8 16.0 s, automatic 15.8 s; about 1.3 GB per cloned passage (tests/benchmark_batch.py). The takes are reassembled per line with render_plan, silences included. One seed per request: a batch does not reproduce the per-line seeds of speak, so a voice that must stay the same across lines should be a stable voice.

Results are written after every group (resultats.json, resultats.csv), so an interrupted task keeps what it finished; resume skips every line marked ok whose WAV still exists and looks the others up again (a character created since is found). The global execution lock still holds: a task is one job, and the parallelism is inside the model's batch, not across processes.

ComfyUI#

app/comfyui/cytools_personarp is a ComfyUI node pack; personarp/comfyui.py installs it (install_comfyui_nodes, filesystemExternal) into the custom_nodes of a ComfyUI given as its folder, a base directory or custom_nodes itself, and finds Comfy Desktop installations from installations.json (adoptedBaseDir, basePath, installPath). The copy is staged and swapped in whole; config.json names the Tool; comfyui_nodes_status compares the digest of the files really installed with the source.

The pack never imports the Tool (a test forbids it): client.py, standard library only, speaks the CyTools protocol to tool.py --data-dir data/jobs-comfyui serve --port 8791 — its own job store, since two runtimes cannot own one — with a token from tool.py create-client (filesystemExternal, network) kept in data/settings/comfyui-client.json. It starts the server on the first node that runs, never on a menu (menus read data/personas, data/voices and the catalogues while the server is down), probes it with GetCapabilities, never starts a second one, and stops it at exit with the whole process tree — on Windows the venv's python.exe is a launcher whose child is the real server. Jobs follow ComfyUI's progress bar; ComfyUI's interruption cancels them. GPU nodes can unload_all_models() first and call unload_model / release_voice after. AUDIO is {'waveform': [1, C, T], 'sample_rate'}; takes are copied into ComfyUI's output/personarp.

GetRuntimeStatus answered InternalError in CyToolsCore 0.9.0; 0.10.0 fixed it (the release acceptance reads it over MCP). The nodes still probe the server with GetCapabilities.

Colab#

app/build_colab.py builds CyTools_PersonaRP_Colab beside the Tool: outil/app (the Tool without gui/, desktop.py, the UI helpers, tests/, Docs/, locales/), LICENCES/, the runner app/colab/personarp_colab.py, a notebook generated by the build script (one source), app/colab/LISEZ-MOI.md and an example task. It refuses to build if a weight file slipped in, and rebuilding leaves taches/, modeles/ and resultats/ alone.

The runner copies the Tool to the Colab disk, installs it and runs setup_engine.py voice (falling back to virtualenv where venv has no ensurepip). modeles downloads with the Tool's own CLI — tool.py create-client (network, filesystemExternal; the token is kept on the Colab disk and passed as CYTOOLS_TOKEN, never in argv or on Drive) then tool.py invoke install_voice_model — copies the model to Drive through .part files, verifies size and SHA-256 there and drops the local copy. Every other command runs the Runtime in process with PERSONARP_MODELS_DIR and PERSONARP_BATCHES_DIR on Drive (paths._location accepts absolute paths only). essai speaks one line and keeps the first precision whose take is usable (auto, then float32). lancer records resultats/_taches.json so a new session resumes an interrupted task with speak_batch resume.

precision (auto, bfloat16, float16, float32) reaches the worker, which resolves auto from the compute capability (bfloat16 from 8.0, float16 below, float32 on the CPU) and keys the resident model by dtype.

Photographs and the vision pass#

A sheet carries references[]: photographs copied into data/personas/<id>.images, each with its role, caption, pixel size and SHA-256. imaging.verify reports a picture that has moved or changed. They are export material and vision input; prompting never puts them in front of the roleplay model.

describe_image reads one downscaled picture (long edge 1024, JPEG) in two passes on the same resident vision model:

  • look — the picture with authoring.observation_request(), no grammar: 150 to 300 words of English prose, garment by garment. A single pass constrained to JSON answered one word per field (« longue », « bleus »): the grammar let the model stop as soon as a field was technically filled. The observation is returned as observation.
  • write — text only, authoring.vision_request(..., observation=) under authoring.vision_schema(): every field required but allowed empty (optional fields were skipped although the observation described them), a minimum length on summary, hair, eyes and outfit, six to twelve tags of at least twelve characters with a good and a bad list (« jeune femme », « yeux bleus » are true of thousands of people), one language only. authoring.clean_vision_fields then removes CJK characters from a sheet in another language (Qwen drifts into Chinese now and then), stuttered words and repeated tags.

The assistant's picture context gets both the fields and the observation.

The result is a proposal applied through apply_proposal, so a photograph can never overwrite a branch you did not ask it to.

resident.ensure passes --mmproj when the catalogue entry declares one, and --no-mmproj-auto otherwise so llama-server never fetches a projector by itself. The projector path is part of the resident key, and the history-fitting pass is skipped for a multimodal call because re-templating a message that carries an image does not survive.

The data model#

A persona is one JSON document validated by PERSONA_SCHEMA. Branches: appearance, personality, speech, background, state, memory, relationships, voice, media, generation. state and memory are the parts meant to change as a story advances; everything else is the character.

A world is a separate document holding the lore several personas share. A persona points at one through world_id. library.cast(world_id) returns the others, which the prompt mentions so a character does not invent people who already exist.

Every save writes a new revision and archives the previous document under <id>.revisions/. remove moves to .trash. Nothing is ever deleted by an operation.

Identifiers are readable slugs (nymphaea), validated against [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,79}; anything else is refused before it can reach the filesystem.

Prompt assembly#

prompting.messages() builds the system prompt in priority order and drops the least essential sections when the character's context_budget is exceeded. The identity section is never dropped. What was dropped is returned in context.droppedSections, so the interface can say so instead of degrading the character silently. A second, tokenizer-based pass (context_window.fit_messages) then fits the real model context once the server is up.

Past assistant turns are cleaned before they go back into the prompt: the scene directive is removed and the delivery annotations are stripped. Leaving the directive in would teach the model to answer in JSON.

The scene directive#

Two modes, on media.mode:

  • director (default) — the roleplay model writes only the reply. A second call, with json_schema set from scene.director_schema(), asks a storyboard prompt for the shot. llama.cpp compiles that schema into a decoding grammar, so the JSON is always parseable. The directive is then run through scene.sanitize_directive(), which clamps ranges a grammar cannot express (a negative timestamp, a 900-second clip) instead of discarding a whole description over one bad float.
  • inline — the instruction is appended to the roleplay prompt and the reply is parsed with scene.split_reply(). One generation instead of two, but small models often skip it.

The director prompt receives only visual facts. Memory, secrets and the conversation history are deliberately excluded: they are not what a camera sees.

media.director_model selects a different installed model for the description pass. The first pass is forced to keep_loaded while a director pass follows, and the caller's real preference is applied once, afterwards.

Voice annotations#

[tone: …], [ton: …], [pause: 400ms], [émotion: …], [rate: …], [volume: …], [murmure] and their English spellings map to one canonical kind in scene.KINDS. Unknown brackets are left alone, so ordinary prose in square brackets survives. scene.tidy() closes the gap a removed mark leaves, because "Bonjour ." is an audible pause in a speech backend.

Example worlds#

app/examples/NN-<world>.zip are ordinary export bundles — one world, its cast and one locked stable voice per character with its reference recording — listed by list_examples (personarp/examples.py) and imported with import_personas. They ship with the application rather than in data/ because an import is a copy. import_bundle remaps the bonds between characters imported together when one of them has to take a new identifier, so importing an example twice gives two casts that point at themselves. tests/test_examples.py validates every bundle against the schemas, checks every bond target, imports each twice, and runs each sheet through prompting.messages — the chat's own path, which gives the sheet 70 % of context_budget — to prove nothing is dropped; tests/acceptance_examples.py plays two of them with the real model in a temporary library. build_example_voices.py produces those voices: a take per character invented by VoiceDesign from the sheet's voice description and the character's own words, transcribed back by Whisper and recaptured with another seed below 80 % of the words heard, registered as a stable voice and re-exported with the recording. It works in runtime/build/example-voices, never in data/, and skips a character that already has its voice, so it can be stopped and resumed. --takes <folder> takes ready-made <persona-id>.wav + .txt instead (no GPU).

Importing a voice never touches one already in the library: the same recording (same SHA-256) is reused, a different voice under the same name comes in as <id>-2, and the imported sheets follow the new identifier.

Optional object parameters (an inline sheet, a mirror bond, a voice override) carry no default in the manifest: the validator would expand {} into a complete blank document that then replaces the real one. optional() and partial() in build_manifest.py build them, and a test forbids a defaulted optional object.

Interface#

The window is drawn with CyUI, the CyTools interface library, through its Python port app/cyui.py plus selected app/cyui_modules/ sources, unchanged at the revision in app/cyui-source.json; refresh with app/scripts/sync_cyui.py rather than manual copying. A top bar carries the selected character, unsaved edits and the running job with its cancel button; a sidebar groups the pages (Roleplay, Create, Voice, Library, System, Tool); a status bar keeps the last operation and notice; the audio player sits above it while a take is loaded. Settings are property tables (label left, control right) in sections, each page has at most one accent button, toolbar actions are icons with tooltips, and an empty page says why and what to do. gui/widgets.py holds the field helpers: inside with widgets.properties('##id'): they become property rows. Theme (five CyUI themes) and density (compact or comfortable) are chosen in Options. --ui-test-theme=<key> draws another theme for a screenshot without saving it.

Interface languages#

English is the default; French is chosen in Options. Every string the window shows is looked up in app/locales/ui.json. tests/locale_strings.py reads the window's code the way it translates it — facade labels, shared widgets, tr(), notices, loop captions, *_CAPTIONS constants and the progress steps jobs report — and tests/test_locale.py fails when a string has no French, when a label is formatted or concatenated before translation (no entry could match it), or when a French string changes on a second translation. Translate a template before formatting it: tr('Take of %.1f s ready.') % seconds, never the formatted result.

What this build does not do#

No Linux runtime. A physical microphone was not recorded by the tests (the recorder is tested with a simulated one), Colab itself has not run the notebook yet (its cells now leave a journal and a report to send back), and no update has gone from one published release to the next. The acceptance runs write their evidence to data/reports/ (local, never committed); VALIDATION.md there is the authority on what has actually been executed; it also lists the defects the acceptance runs found and the fixes they produced.

Contracts followed#

Docs/StandaloneDelivery.md (clean root, real ImGui window, guided model installation, GitHub updates with rollback), Docs/SharedInstallation.md (private Python, no automatic model relocation — the migration here was an explicit, receipted, reversible action), Docs/Localization.md (English by default, French selectable, Options tab from the SDK), Docs/GenerationConfigurations.md (save/load the current configuration).

Application icon#

The logo source is assets/branding/logo.png. build_icon.ps1 derives the 16-256 px Windows ICO and assets/app_settings/icon.png for Hello ImGui. build_launcher.ps1 embeds the ICO in the launcher. branding.py selects assets independently of the working directory and assigns this Tool its own Windows taskbar identity.

Modular CyUI#

The standalone interface uses the pinned, selected CyUI 1.2 modules. See the migration and validation notes for replacements, retained host adaptations, source hashes and reproducible refresh instructions.
pages.text: CyTools_PersonaRP — developer documentation # Documentation · Français cy.tool.personarp , built on CyToolsCore 0.10.1. Local roleplay with persistent characters, a shared world, relationships, and machine-readable scene descriptions for image and video tools. No model is part of the repository: engines and weights are downloaded from the interface (Models tab, Voice tab), each at a pinned revision and verified by SHA-256. License: GPL-3.0-only ( ../LICENSE ). It covers the code, the window, the ComfyUI node pack (which carries its own copy of the licence), the Colab project and the example worlds. The SDK, CyToolsCore 0.10.1, is MIT: ../LICENCES/CyToolsCore-MIT.txt and LICENSE-CyToolsCore.txt (the notice the 0.10.1 scaffold puts beside a Tool's code) hold its full text, and ../LICENCES/SOURCES.txt lists the sources of every component. LICENCES/ is in git, in the release zip (with Python-Runtime-Notices.txt written by build_release.py ) and in the Colab project. Model weights are downloaded separately under their own licences ( licenses.json , llm-catalog.json , tts-catalog.json ). Install, build, run # text Copy py -3.11 -m venv runtime/python cd app && ../runtime/python/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -r requirements.txt The requirement file installs CyToolsCore 0.10.1 (MIT) from its public repository, https://github.com/MrMybal/CyToolsCore , pinned to commit a8d200f2d0ba — the code this Tool was migrated to and verified against. git must be on the PATH : pip clones that commit. Going back to 0.1.1 means its commit and its requirement (CyToolsCore 0.9.0 at 442f53740fc6 ); release.json carries runtime_abi python311-cytools010-… , so the Updates tab refuses to put this application on a runtime that still has the 0.9 SDK, which would ignore the exclusion groups.
