Never edit it by hand: a test compares the published manifest with the generator's output, because a stale manifest silently rejects valid documents through output validation. Layout # text Copy app/ tool.py Runtime and every operation handler desktop.py Dear ImGui window: top bar, sidebar, pages, status bar cyui.py CyUI for Python (copy of CyImgui_Interface/python/cyui.py) build_manifest.py generates CyTool.json from the schemas llm-catalog.json conversation models: repo, pinned revision, size, SHA-256, licence personarp/ paths.py folders, atomic JSON read/write schemas.py persona, world, relation, scene, voice — the portable contract library.py collections, revisions, trash, relationships, export/import batches.py voice batches: parsing, speaker lookup, folders, results sessions.py saved conversations prompting.py prompt assembly, context budget, director prompt scene.py reply parsing, annotations, directive schema and sanitising authoring.py the creation assistant models.py catalogue, installation state, download, engine paths resident.py the owned llama.cpp server context_window.py tokenizer-based history fitting derived.py writing-style output head applied to a private copy of a base model maintenance.py GitHub updates: stage, verify, activate, roll back locks.py cross-process locks marks.py the delivery-mark vocabulary, standard library only workerhost.py persistent worker processes over JSON lines voice/ catalog.py speech models and the private engine annotations.py marks compiled into a plan of passages and silences stable.py stable voices: create, verify, lock, trash delivery.py which voice, which mode, which weights, which instruction runner.py the worker pool bound to the runtime batching.py batch sizing and out-of-memory backoff, standard library only workers/ _protocol.py, tts_worker.py, stt_worker.py — run in the voice engine gui/ state.py, widgets.py, panels.py, voice_panel.py, batch_panel.py, player.py tests/ pytest suite, MCP acceptance, speech and batch acceptance examples/lots/ example batches (script, CSV, JSON) for the Valdrenn cast Two environments # runtime/python is the Tool's own light environment: the SDK, Dear ImGui, soundfile. The speech stack lives apart in runtime/engines/voice (PyTorch CUDA, Qwen3-TTS, Whisper, about 8 GB), built by app/setup_engine.py at its final path and never moved. Nothing heavy is imported by the window, the CLI or the MCP server: the workers in app/workers run inside the engine and talk over the JSON-lines protocol in personarp/workerhost.py . The workers import personarp.voice.annotations and nothing else of ours, which is why the mark vocabulary sits in personarp/marks.py on the standard library alone — the SDK is not installed in the engine. Speed, pitch and takes # personarp/voice/prosody.py applies the sheet's voice.speed (0.25–4) and voice.pitch (±12 semitones) after the model, in numpy: WSOLA time-stretching by pitch-ratio/speed, then an FFT resampling to the target length, one pass each. _render_voice shapes every segment of a take and rebuilds the whole line and its timeline; _speak_batch shapes each line with its own speaker's settings; capture_voice_take neutralises both, so a stable voice is never cloned from a shaped take. Measured on a real 18 s take: durations exact, fundamental within 1 %, 0.05–0.2 s of processing. personarp/takes.py : a line's audio record (turn, or translation) keeps its old shape for the chosen take and lists every take under takes . speak_turn writes a new file ( turn-NNN-<lang>-<stamp>.wav ) and chooses it; choose_take and remove_take (to audio/<session>/.trash ) take the execution lock, since a generation rewrites the whole scene when it saves. A record from before takes existed counts as one take. A retranslated line sends the takes of its old words to the trash. Microphone and dictation # gui/recorder.py records from the chosen input (the default input's audio API only, so a device is listed once) at 24 kHz, or at the card's own rate when it refuses, into data/inputs/micro-<purpose>-<stamp>.wav ; nothing is opened before a button is pressed. The Voice tab records a take (stops at 30 s) for create_stable_voice ; the Scene tab's Dictate records up to 2 minutes and submits transcribe , whose text is appended to the message. No operation opens the microphone: from the CLI or MCP, transcribe takes a file. Messages in the window's language # Operations answer in English for every interface. locales/messages.json holds each message as the code writes it, variable parts as {0} , {1} …; personarp/messages.templates() reads them from the code (raises, returned reasons, reason += , problems, notes), and tests/test_messages.py fails when one has no French. gui.state.shown() translates what the window shows — errors (the code stays visible in brackets), notices, progress steps, batch problems and line errors — matching the whole message and translating variable parts that are messages themselves (a reason followed by its consequence, a language name). Jobs and the execution lock # The manifest declares Concurrent (16 workers): the window waits for the answer of a list, a sheet or a session ( AppState.call ), and under Sequential those requests queued behind a voice being spoken — the window stopped drawing, Windows declared it hung, and closing it lost the voice already generated. Every job that uses the GPU or stops an engine ( chat , speak* , translate , describe_image , installations, update , unload_model , release_voice , the take operations — 21 in all) takes personarp.locks.exclusive and is declared in the SDK's gpu exclusion group (CyToolsCore 0.10, operations[].exclusiveGroups ): the runtime itself keeps the next ones Queued, in order, cancellable, without a worker slot. personarp/exclusion.py reads that list from tool.py (handlers and wrappers that take the lock) and build_manifest.py writes it, so the two cannot drift. The lock no longer queues anything: it keeps other processes out (the window and an MCP server have separate runtimes, which the groups do not coordinate) and lets a job that holds it take it again (the maintenance wrapper, then its handler). tests/test_concurrency.py checks that the grouped list equals what the code locks, that the installed SDK enforces groups, that a list is answered at once while a job holds the lock, that a second job stays Queued then runs, that a queued job can be cancelled, that unloading the model waits for the generation, and that another process gets Busy . The binary release # app/build_release.py builds the release from the commit HEAD ( git archive ; uncommitted changes are refused) into runtime/build/release/<version>/ . In the portable zip, runtime/python is not a virtual environment but a private CPython 3.11, copied from an official installation without site-packages, byte-code, Tk, IDLE or the test suite. Its interpreter and the DLLs it loads live in runtime/python/Scripts , so every path the Tool already uses (the launcher, the manifest's executable , the ComfyUI nodes, the voice engine setup) finds it where a virtual environment would put it; Python finds Lib/ by searching upwards from the executable. runtime/python/pyvenv.cfg holds only include-system-site-packages = false : with no home line the interpreter keeps its own folder as prefix, and site (frozen into the 3.11 executable, so editing Lib/site.py would change nothing) turns the per-user site-packages off, so a user's own packages never shadow the Tool's. Packages are installed at the versions of the development runtime (constraints from its pip freeze ), console-script wrappers (which hold the absolute path of the build machine) and every __pycache__ are removed, runtime/python/THIRD-PARTY.md lists each package and its licence, and runtime/build-info.json records the commit and the versions. The build fails if the packaged interpreter reads anything outside the package, or if any file of the package names the project folder, the base Python, the user profile (long or 8.3 form) or the machine name. The voice engine is created from this interpreter with venv , which the copy keeps. app/tests/acceptance_release.py extracts the zip into a new folder with a space in its name and runs it with PATH reduced to Windows, no PYTHON* variable and a working directory outside the package: layout, interpreter isolation (including a module planted in a per-user site-packages, which must stay invisible while the machine's own CPython, the control, imports it), the CLI, a real MCP session whose client is granted filesystemExternal and imports an example world, the launcher opening two tabs, a venv made from the private interpreter, and with --tests the whole suite inside the copy. Voice # A capability is a set of weights, not a flag. Qwen3-TTS ships one variant per capability and refuses the others outright, so delivery.VARIANTS maps the mode to the weights and _model_for substitutes with an explanation rather than letting the model answer with a message about tokenizer types: Mode Weights Used when clone 1.7B-Base , 0.6B-Base a stable voice is attached — the normal case design 1.7B-VoiceDesign the sheet carries a written voice description custom 1.7B-CustomVoice , 0.6B-CustomVoice a preset speaker A stable voice is a document in data/voices holding the reference recording, its exact transcript, its SHA-256 and the variant that reads it. It is locked on creation: changing the reference or the model is refused, because a voice that quietly changes is worse than no voice. verify_voice reports a moved or modified recording. The take produced by capture_voice_take is copied to data/voices/takes before the job workspace disappears, so it can still be registered later. spoken_text decides what reaches the worker: the scene directive never does, narration does only when the sheet says so, and annotations are kept only for a backend that understands them. generate_voice_clone has no instruction input, so in clone mode the acting direction and the tone marks are built but not read by the model; only pauses (rendered as silence by the plan) reach a cloned voice. The sheet says so next to the stable voice picker. Languages # voice.language on the sheet is the character's own language and wins over the language recorded on the stable voice ( delivery.native_language ). voice.languages[] holds one entry per other language ( LANGUAGE_VOICE_SCHEMA ), and payload_for(..., language=) applies it: source What speaks Mode same , accent: keep (also: no entry) the main voice; the in-context clone carries the take's accent clone , full reference same , accent: native the main voice's timbre only clone , x_vector_only voice another stable voice, typically captured in that language clone design a voice invented from the entry's description design preset a preset speaker with the entry's direction custom Without a stable voice, same asks for the accent in the instruction instead. A missing per-language voice falls back to the main voice with a note, never silently. The payload's voice_plan (returned as voicePlan ) says what was really used. Every translation request carries translation.context_block() — the world (genre, tone, summary, setting; places, factions and glossary terms, those the batch mentions first), who speaks and how (personality, speech style, register, vocabulary, accent, tics), the sheet's current state (situation, place, time, mood), the session title and the caller's context note — bounded to 3 000 characters, and translation.earlier_lines() : the four turns before the batch in their original words, with their translation when one exists or was just made. The system prompt says the context is for understanding only. A text given with a session_id is translated with that scene as context and nothing is stored; world_id gives a text without a character its world. Measured with tests/acceptance_translation_context.py . The lexicon. world.term_translations[<Language>][<term>] = {text, source: model|person, model, at} . translation.world_terms() lists the glossary terms, locations and factions; mentioned_terms() finds them in a text (accent- and case-folded, whole words, a plural s/x allowed). Terms mentioned but not yet rendered go through one constrained pass ( terms_messages , terms_schema — the meaning is a hint, a rendering is bounded to a name's length) and parse_terms keeps only plausible names (no sentence, a leading article lower-cased); they are recorded in the world unless keep_terms is off. Each batch then gets the renderings of the terms it uses as names ( used_as_name : a compound always, a single word only where it is capitalised), missed_terms checks the answer (article dropped, plural and possessive allowed), a line that dropped one is asked again once with insist , and what is still missing is stored as termsMissed on the turn. save_world keeps the lexicon on disk (a window's older copy cannot wipe it); it changes through translate and set_term_translations only ( source: person is never replaced), and translation_terms reads it. A first version of the terms prompt presented the meaning beside the term and a 4B model translated the meaning; tests/acceptance_translation_terms.py now fails on a description-like rendering. translate (see personarp/translation.py ) masks the delivery marks as ⟦n⟧ tokens, batches turns up to 2 400 characters, constrains the answer to one non-empty string per turn, restores the marks and reports any the model lost. Translations are stored beside the turn ( turn.translations[<Language>] = {text, model, at, marksLost, audio?} ); the original is never rewritten, already translated turns are skipped unless overwrite , and a changed translation drops the take made from the old words. speak_turn speaks a stored line in its own language or a translation and keeps the take under data/sessions/<persona>/audio/<session>/ . create_stable_voice with for_language attaches a voice to that language only; capture_voice_take ignores the per-language entries so a take is always the voice described. Batch tasks # speak_batch (list inline: text as a script, CSV or JSON — format auto-detects — or items , or resume ) and speak_batch_file (anything read from disk: file , personas , use_library ; filesystemExternal ) share one handler. The split exists because permissions are per operation: an AI client with no permission must be able to send its lines, while reading an arbitrary file stays reserved, like import_personas . list_batches lists data/batches . Tasks are ordinary jobs: several submitted in a row wait behind the runtime's Sequential policy, and the window queues them in App.pending . A task's own characters. personas are bundles exported by export_personas with the recordings. batches.import_task_personas copies them into <task>/personnages/ ( fiches/ , mondes/ , voix-stables/ with each recording and a relative path, import.json ) and never into the library; within the task a taken identifier gets a new one and the sheets follow it. A voice without its recording, or whose recording does not match reference_sha256 , is refused and listed in problems . batches.load_task reads them back — on every run, resume included — and checks each recording against its fingerprint again. delivery.payload_for takes these voices as voices= ; _stable looks there before the library. Cast searches the task's sheets first, then the library unless use_library is off; the source of each speaker ( task , library , voice ) is recorded on the line so a resume speaks with the same one. library.voice_ids / _voice_documents export the per-language voices as well as the main one — before, an exported character lost its English voice. Line ids. batches.assign_ids gives every line its own id (CSV id column, JSON id , script ID | Name: text ) or its number; a repeated id (case-insensitive, as on Windows) is reported on the second line instead of overwriting the first take. file_stem names the take after the id ( safe_name keeps SC01_L005 as it is, reserved device names are prefixed). The handler ( tool.py , _speak_batch ) parses ( personarp/batches.py ), finds each speaker (identifier, name, alias, then a run of whole words only one name holds — an ambiguous name is an error, never a guess), builds each line's payload with delivery.payload_for exactly as speak does, and groups the lines by (mode, model) : one worker request per set of weights. dry_run stops there and returns the plan; it imports the task's characters into the job's own workspace, makes no task folder, takes no lock and reserves no VRAM. The worker ( synthesize_batch in workers/tts_worker.py ) loads the weights once, cuts every line into its plan, pools the passages of all lines longest first ( personarp/voice/batching.py ) and calls generate_voice_clone / generate_voice_design / generate_custom_voice with lists — Qwen3-TTS batches them in one forward pass, each with its own voice prompt, language and instruction. One clone prompt is encoded per reference, however many lines use it. batch_size 0 measures instead of guessing: a first batch of PROBE_BATCH (4) passages — the longest, so the dearest — gives the cost of one passage ( max_memory_allocated above the weights), and fit sizes the next batches from the room left ( SAFETY 0.85, 32 at most). The worker caps its allocator with set_per_process_memory_fraction at what was free when it started, minus 1.5 GiB: on Windows the driver otherwise spills into system memory instead of failing — a first version asked for 26 GB on a 24 GB card and ran 3.7 times slower than one line at a time. Under the cap an oversized batch raises out-of-memory, is halved and retried, and never grows again ( generate_all ). The cap is lifted after the batch so single takes are not limited. Measured on an RTX 3090, 16 cloned lines: size 1 76.5 s, 4 26.4 s, 8 16.0 s, automatic 15.8 s; about 1.3 GB per cloned passage ( tests/benchmark_batch.py ). The takes are reassembled per line with render_plan , silences included. One seed per request: a batch does not reproduce the per-line seeds of speak , so a voice that must stay the same across lines should be a stable voice. Results are written after every group ( resultats.json , resultats.csv ), so an interrupted task keeps what it finished; resume skips every line marked ok whose WAV still exists and looks the others up again (a character created since is found). The global execution lock still holds: a task is one job, and the parallelism is inside the model's batch, not across processes. ComfyUI # app/comfyui/cytools_personarp is a ComfyUI node pack; personarp/comfyui.py installs it ( install_comfyui_nodes , filesystemExternal ) into the custom_nodes of a ComfyUI given as its folder, a base directory or custom_nodes itself, and finds Comfy Desktop installations from installations.json ( adoptedBaseDir , basePath , installPath ). The copy is staged and swapped in whole; config.json names the Tool; comfyui_nodes_status compares the digest of the files really installed with the source. The pack never imports the Tool (a test forbids it): client.py , standard library only, speaks the CyTools protocol to tool.py --data-dir data/jobs-comfyui serve --port 8791 — its own job store, since two runtimes cannot own one — with a token from tool.py create-client (filesystemExternal, network) kept in data/settings/comfyui-client.json . It starts the server on the first node that runs, never on a menu (menus read data/personas , data/voices and the catalogues while the server is down), probes it with GetCapabilities , never starts a second one, and stops it at exit with the whole process tree — on Windows the venv's python.exe is a launcher whose child is the real server. Jobs follow ComfyUI's progress bar; ComfyUI's interruption cancels them. GPU nodes can unload_all_models() first and call unload_model / release_voice after. AUDIO is {'waveform': [1, C, T], 'sample_rate'} ; takes are copied into ComfyUI's output/personarp . GetRuntimeStatus answered InternalError in CyToolsCore 0.9.0; 0.10.0 fixed it (the release acceptance reads it over MCP). The nodes still probe the server with GetCapabilities . Colab # app/build_colab.py builds CyTools_PersonaRP_Colab beside the Tool: outil/app (the Tool without gui/ , desktop.py , the UI helpers, tests/ , Docs/ , locales/ ), LICENCES/ , the runner app/colab/personarp_colab.py , a notebook generated by the build script (one source), app/colab/LISEZ-MOI.md and an example task. It refuses to build if a weight file slipped in, and rebuilding leaves taches/ , modeles/ and resultats/ alone. The runner copies the Tool to the Colab disk, installs it and runs setup_engine.py voice (falling back to virtualenv where venv has no ensurepip ). modeles downloads with the Tool's own CLI — tool.py create-client (network, filesystemExternal; the token is kept on the Colab disk and passed as CYTOOLS_TOKEN , never in argv or on Drive) then tool.py invoke install_voice_model — copies the model to Drive through .part files, verifies size and SHA-256 there and drops the local copy. Every other command runs the Runtime in process with PERSONARP_MODELS_DIR and PERSONARP_BATCHES_DIR on Drive ( paths._location accepts absolute paths only). essai speaks one line and keeps the first precision whose take is usable (auto, then float32). lancer records resultats/_taches.json so a new session resumes an interrupted task with speak_batch resume . precision ( auto , bfloat16 , float16 , float32 ) reaches the worker, which resolves auto from the compute capability (bfloat16 from 8.0, float16 below, float32 on the CPU) and keys the resident model by dtype. Photographs and the vision pass # A sheet carries references[] : photographs copied into data/personas/<id>.images , each with its role, caption, pixel size and SHA-256. imaging.verify reports a picture that has moved or changed. They are export material and vision input; prompting never puts them in front of the roleplay model. describe_image reads one downscaled picture (long edge 1024, JPEG) in two passes on the same resident vision model: look — the picture with authoring.observation_request() , no grammar: 150 to 300 words of English prose, garment by garment. A single pass constrained to JSON answered one word per field (« longue », « bleus »): the grammar let the model stop as soon as a field was technically filled. The observation is returned as observation . write — text only, authoring.vision_request(..., observation=) under authoring.vision_schema() : every field required but allowed empty (optional fields were skipped although the observation described them), a minimum length on summary, hair, eyes and outfit, six to twelve tags of at least twelve characters with a good and a bad list (« jeune femme », « yeux bleus » are true of thousands of people), one language only. authoring.clean_vision_fields then removes CJK characters from a sheet in another language (Qwen drifts into Chinese now and then), stuttered words and repeated tags. The assistant's picture context gets both the fields and the observation. The result is a proposal applied through apply_proposal , so a photograph can never overwrite a branch you did not ask it to. resident.ensure passes --mmproj when the catalogue entry declares one, and --no-mmproj-auto otherwise so llama-server never fetches a projector by itself. The projector path is part of the resident key, and the history-fitting pass is skipped for a multimodal call because re-templating a message that carries an image does not survive. The data model # A persona is one JSON document validated by PERSONA_SCHEMA . Branches: appearance , personality , speech , background , state , memory , relationships , voice , media , generation . state and memory are the parts meant to change as a story advances; everything else is the character. A world is a separate document holding the lore several personas share. A persona points at one through world_id . library.cast(world_id) returns the others, which the prompt mentions so a character does not invent people who already exist. Every save writes a new revision and archives the previous document under <id>.revisions/ . remove moves to .trash . Nothing is ever deleted by an operation. Identifiers are readable slugs ( nymphaea ), validated against [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,79} ; anything else is refused before it can reach the filesystem. Prompt assembly # prompting.messages() builds the system prompt in priority order and drops the least essential sections when the character's context_budget is exceeded. The identity section is never dropped. What was dropped is returned in context.droppedSections , so the interface can say so instead of degrading the character silently. A second, tokenizer-based pass ( context_window.fit_messages ) then fits the real model context once the server is up. Past assistant turns are cleaned before they go back into the prompt: the scene directive is removed and the delivery annotations are stripped. Leaving the directive in would teach the model to answer in JSON. The scene directive # Two modes, on media.mode : director (default) — the roleplay model writes only the reply. A second call, with json_schema set from scene.director_schema() , asks a storyboard prompt for the shot. llama.cpp compiles that schema into a decoding grammar, so the JSON is always parseable. The directive is then run through scene.sanitize_directive() , which clamps ranges a grammar cannot express (a negative timestamp, a 900-second clip) instead of discarding a whole description over one bad float. inline — the instruction is appended to the roleplay prompt and the reply is parsed with scene.split_reply() . One generation instead of two, but small models often skip it. The director prompt receives only visual facts. Memory, secrets and the conversation history are deliberately excluded: they are not what a camera sees. media.director_model selects a different installed model for the description pass. The first pass is forced to keep_loaded while a director pass follows, and the caller's real preference is applied once, afterwards. Voice annotations # [tone: …] , [ton: …] , [pause: 400ms] , [émotion: …] , [rate: …] , [volume: …] , [murmure] and their English spellings map to one canonical kind in scene.KINDS . Unknown brackets are left alone, so ordinary prose in square brackets survives. scene.tidy() closes the gap a removed mark leaves, because "Bonjour ." is an audible pause in a speech backend. Example worlds # app/examples/NN-<world>.zip are ordinary export bundles — one world, its cast and one locked stable voice per character with its reference recording — listed by list_examples ( personarp/examples.py ) and imported with import_personas . They ship with the application rather than in data/ because an import is a copy. import_bundle remaps the bonds between characters imported together when one of them has to take a new identifier, so importing an example twice gives two casts that point at themselves. tests/test_examples.py validates every bundle against the schemas, checks every bond target, imports each twice, and runs each sheet through prompting.messages — the chat's own path, which gives the sheet 70 % of context_budget — to prove nothing is dropped; tests/acceptance_examples.py plays two of them with the real model in a temporary library. build_example_voices.py produces those voices: a take per character invented by VoiceDesign from the sheet's voice description and the character's own words, transcribed back by Whisper and recaptured with another seed below 80 % of the words heard, registered as a stable voice and re-exported with the recording. It works in runtime/build/example-voices , never in data/ , and skips a character that already has its voice, so it can be stopped and resumed. --takes <folder> takes ready-made <persona-id>.wav + .txt instead (no GPU). Importing a voice never touches one already in the library: the same recording (same SHA-256) is reused, a different voice under the same name comes in as <id>-2 , and the imported sheets follow the new identifier. Optional object parameters (an inline sheet, a mirror bond, a voice override) carry no default in the manifest: the validator would expand {} into a complete blank document that then replaces the real one. optional() and partial() in build_manifest.py build them, and a test forbids a defaulted optional object. Interface # The window is drawn with CyUI, the CyTools interface library, through its Python port app/cyui.py plus selected app/cyui_modules/ sources, unchanged at the revision in app/cyui-source.json ; refresh with app/scripts/sync_cyui.py rather than manual copying. A top bar carries the selected character, unsaved edits and the running job with its cancel button; a sidebar groups the pages (Roleplay, Create, Voice, Library, System, Tool); a status bar keeps the last operation and notice; the audio player sits above it while a take is loaded. Settings are property tables (label left, control right) in sections, each page has at most one accent button, toolbar actions are icons with tooltips, and an empty page says why and what to do. gui/widgets.py holds the field helpers: inside with widgets.properties('##id'): they become property rows. Theme (five CyUI themes) and density (compact or comfortable) are chosen in Options. --ui-test-theme=<key> draws another theme for a screenshot without saving it. Interface languages # English is the default; French is chosen in Options. Every string the window shows is looked up in app/locales/ui.json . tests/locale_strings.py reads the window's code the way it translates it — facade labels, shared widgets, tr() , notices, loop captions, *_CAPTIONS constants and the progress steps jobs report — and tests/test_locale.py fails when a string has no French, when a label is formatted or concatenated before translation (no entry could match it), or when a French string changes on a second translation. Translate a template before formatting it: tr('Take of %.1f s ready.') % seconds , never the formatted result. What this build does not do # No Linux runtime. A physical microphone was not recorded by the tests (the recorder is tested with a simulated one), Colab itself has not run the notebook yet (its cells now leave a journal and a report to send back), and no update has gone from one published release to the next. pages.title: CyTools PersonaRP
pages.html:
CyTools PersonaRP#

Documentation · Français

Local roleplay with persistent characters, for Windows: a desktop application, a command line and an MCP server on one runtime, built on the CyToolsCore SDK. Characters live in a shared world, remember what you tell them to, speak with a stable voice, and every reply comes with a machine-readable description of what a camera would see. French user guide: LISEZ-MOI.md. Developer guide: app/README.md.

Screenshots#

<table> <tr> <td> ```image {"id": "image-ab09241d8830", "src": "assets/b52def57d3874420-character-model.png", "alt": "Character sheet, Model section: conversation model, device, instructions and sampling", "controls": "minimal"} ``` </td> <td> ```image {"id": "image-cd4faf3a9554", "src": "assets/d01ca19508d74c90-character-voice.png", "alt": "Character sheet, Voice section: stable voice, what is spoken, speed and pitch", "controls": "minimal"} ``` </td> </tr> <tr> <td align="center">Character sheet — model settings</td> <td align="center">Character sheet — voice</td> </tr> <tr> <td> ```image {"id": "image-2c3ee1d3e523", "src": "assets/cdf504ae976e968c-worlds.png", "alt": "Worlds page: cast, world description, places and factions", "controls": "minimal"} ``` </td> <td> ```image {"id": "image-e2fe5c35e87e", "src": "assets/6d746dc339bce1f4-assistant.png", "alt": "Assistant discussion: a picture read by the vision model, and two character ideas", "controls": "minimal"} ``` </td> </tr> <tr> <td align="center">Shared world and its cast</td> <td align="center">Assistant, starting from a picture</td> </tr> </table>

What it does#

  • Characters: a complete sheet (identity, appearance, personality, way of speaking, past, current state, memory, relationships, voice, visual direction, model settings). Every save is a revision; earlier ones are kept and can be restored.
  • Worlds: shared lore (places, factions, laws, timeline, glossary, what must stay true and what never happens). Characters sharing a world know who else lives in it.
  • Relationships with feeling, trust, shared history, tension and secrets; the reverse link can be written on the other sheet automatically.
  • Scenes: one saved conversation per character, resumed later as it was. Memory is explicit: nothing is extracted from a conversation unless you add it.
  • Scene descriptions for image, video and motion tools, generated alongside each reply.
  • Assistant that drafts a sheet, a world or one section of either; nothing is applied until you accept it. It can start from a photograph read by a local vision model (Qwen2.5-VL) under constrained decoding.
  • Voice: Qwen3-TTS (Base, VoiceDesign, CustomVoice), a stable voice captured once from a 12–24 s take (a file, or recorded from the microphone) and cloned for every later line, acting annotations written by the character, a per-character speed and pitch, every take of a line kept (step through them, choose one, send one to the trash), Whisper large-v3 turbo transcription and dictation from the microphone. Runs on an NVIDIA GPU or, more slowly, on the CPU.
  • Translation of a scene with its context (world, character, earlier lines) and a per-world, per-language lexicon so names of places, factions and things stay the same across translations; each language can have its own voice.
  • Voice tasks (batches): import complete characters with their stable voices per language, give a list of lines (script, CSV or JSON, each with an ID), and get one folder per task with every WAV and a results table. Lines are generated several at a time, sized to the free VRAM.
  • Six example worlds, ready to import, each with three or four characters and their voices.
  • ComfyUI nodes (app/comfyui/cytools_personarp), installed from the application, that use the Tool: character, dialogue, voice, scene prompts, translation, reading a photograph, voice tasks.
  • Google Colab project built by app/build_colab.py, for voice tasks on a rented GPU: no model inside, weights downloaded through the Tool's command line and kept on Drive.
  • Models and engines installed from the application (state, size, source, licence, pinned revision, SHA-256 check, cancel and resume) and GitHub updates for the application, the engine and the model catalogue, staged, verified and reversible.

The interface is in English by default and fully in French from Options, including the messages operations send back (errors, notes, update states), which the CLI and MCP keep in English.

Requirements#

  • Windows 10/11 x64 (the only platform executed by the author; a Linux launcher script is provided but was never run). The release archive brings its own Python; installing from source needs Python 3.11 and Git on the PATH.
  • An NVIDIA GPU with CUDA for comfortable use; conversation models also run on the CPU. The speech engine is about 8 GB on disk.
  • Model weights are not in this repository; they are downloaded from the Models and Voice tabs.

Download (Windows x64)#

Each release carries CyTools_PersonaRP-<version>-windows-x64.zip: the launcher, the application and a private Python 3.11 with every package the application needs. Extract it into any folder you can write to, then double-click CyTools_PersonaRP.exe; no Python, git or compiler is needed. Models and engines are not in the archive: install them from the application (see First launch below). Keep the folder where it is once the speech engine is installed, since that engine is a virtual environment tied to its path. SHA256SUMS.txt lists the checksums of the release files; cytools-app.zip is the application alone, used by the Updates tab.

Installation from source#

powershell
git clone https://github.com/MrMybal/CyTools_PersonaRP.gitcd CyTools_PersonaRP# 1. private Python environment of the application (interface, CLI, MCP)py -3.11 -m venv runtime\python.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r app\requirements.txt# 2. Windows launcher (Visual C++ Build Tools)app\build_launcher.cmd

Then double-click CyTools_PersonaRP.exe, or run runtime\python\Scripts\pythonw.exe app\desktop.py. The release archive itself is built with .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\build_release.py and checked with app\tests\acceptance_release.py (see app/README.md).

First launch#

  1. Models tab: install the conversation engine (CUDA or CPU), then at least one conversation model.
  2. Voice tab: install the speech engine, then the speech models you need (1.7B Base for stable voices, VoiceDesign to invent a voice, CustomVoice for preset voices, Whisper to transcribe takes). The speech engine can also be built with .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\setup_engine.py voice.
  3. Optional, Models tab: a vision model to read character photographs.

Command line and MCP#

powershell
.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py describe.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py list-operations.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py invoke chat --params-file request.json.\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe app\tool.py mcp          # MCP stdio server

Input paths must be absolute. Operations that download or read files outside the Tool need the matching permission (create-client --permission network, filesystemExternal); the interface has them.

Repository layout#

text
CyTools_PersonaRP.exe   Windows launcher (built locally, not in git)CyTools_PersonaRP.sh    Linux launcher (never executed by the author)LICENCES/               licence texts and sources: CyToolsCore (MIT), SOURCES.txtLISEZ-MOI.md            user guide (French)app/                    code, manifest (CyTool.json), interface, workers, tests, docs,                        example worlds, ComfyUI nodes, Colab project sourcesdata/                   characters, worlds, scenes, voices, models, tasks, jobs, logs (not in git)runtime/                private Python, engines, staged updates, backups (not in git)

Tests (fixtures only, no GPU): .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install pytest, then .\runtime\python\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest app\tests -q. What was actually executed is recorded in data/reports/VALIDATION.md of an installation and summarised at the end of LISEZ-MOI.md.

Licence#

Free software under the GNU General Public License v3.0 only (LICENSE). This covers the code, the interface, the ComfyUI nodes, the Colab project and the example worlds. The Tool is built on the CyToolsCore 0.10.1 SDK, licensed under MIT (Copyright (c) 2026 Cyberalien): full text in LICENCES/CyToolsCore-MIT.txt, sources of every component in LICENCES/SOURCES.txt. Engines and model weights keep their own licences, listed in app/licenses.json, in the model catalogues and in the Options tab; the Models tab asks for acceptance before downloading. Releases 0.1.0 and 0.1.1 were built on CyToolsCore 0.9.0 under GPL-3.0-only; copies received under that licence keep it.

Modular CyUI#

The standalone interface uses the pinned, selected CyUI 1.2 modules. See the migration and validation notes for replacements, retained host adaptations, source hashes and reproducible refresh instructions.

CyUI: MIT. Full license: LICENCES/CyUI-MIT.txt. Upstream license: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI/blob/main/LICENSE Repository: https://github.com/MrMybal/CyUI (currently private; no upstream access required to run this application).

Local documentation#

Open Options → Open local manual (F1) or press F1 in the application. The complete offline reader is shipped in app/help/index.html. Regenerate the manual.

Source documentation#

Python AST public definitions are imported using CyDoc’s neutral API format. CyDoc provides a lexical index of the distributed tool.py, not a semantic Python compiler.

pages.title: create_stable_voice
pages.html:
Register a recording as a reusable voice. Every later line of that character is cloned from this take, so the voice stops drifting between replies and between sessions. The exact words of the take are required; they can be transcribed here.

pages.title: describe_image
pages.html:
Read a reference photograph with a vision model and return the appearance branch: build, face, hair, eyes, skin, outfit, marks, accessories, and the visual tags that every later image prompt repeats word for word. Two passes: the model first describes the picture in free prose (returned as observation, in English), then writes the fields from that observation in the language asked, as phrases rather than single words. The result is a proposal — apply it with apply_proposal.

pages.html:
speak_batch, with files: the list read from file (a script .txt, a CSV .csv/.tsv or a JSON list .json; text or items still work), and personas, the characters the task brings — bundles exported by PersonaRP with their recordings (sheet, world, stable voices, the per-language ones included). They are copied into the task folder (personnages/) and never into the library, and are looked up before the library; use_library false keeps the task to its own characters. The folder holds the list as given (source.*), the batch as understood (lot.json), one WAV per line in voix/, and resultats.json / resultats.csv. The lines are generated many at a time in one copy of the voice model; with batch_size 0 the number follows the free VRAM, and a batch that does not fit is halved and tried again, so a large GPU is used to the full. A speaker is found by identifier, name, alias or a part of its name no other character has; voice names a stable voice instead, or on top of the character. A line that cannot be spoken is reported and the batch goes on. dry_run checks the list — speakers, voices, languages — before paying for it.

pages.title: speak_batch
pages.html:
Speak a list of lines — who says what — into a new task folder of data/batches. The list is sent inline: text holds a script ("Name: line", or "ID | Name: line"), a CSV or a JSON list (format auto recognises them), or items gives the lines as objects. Every line gets an id — its own, or its number — and its take is named after it. The folder holds the list as given (source.*), the batch as understood (lot.json), one WAV per line in voix/, and resultats.json / resultats.csv. The lines are generated many at a time in one copy of the voice model; with batch_size 0 the number follows the free VRAM, and a batch that does not fit is halved and tried again, so a large GPU is used to the full. A speaker is found by identifier, name, alias or a part of its name no other character has; voice names a stable voice instead, or on top of the character. pages.title: translate
pages.html:
Translate a stored scene, or a single text, with a language model of your choice. The translation is written beside each turn — the original is never changed — so a scene can carry several languages. Delivery marks such as [ton: ...] or [pause: 400ms] are masked before translation and put back afterwards; any the model loses are reported. The answer is constrained to one string per turn. Every request carries the context the words need, never translated itself: the world (genre, tone, setting, the places, factions and terms mentioned first), who speaks and how, where the scene stands, the lines just before in their original words, and your own note in context. A text given together with session_id is translated in the light of that scene, and nothing is stored. The places, factions and terms of the world read the same in every translation: each is rendered once per language, recorded in the world (term_translations; see translation_terms), required in every request, and a line that drops one is asked again once — termsMissed reports what still does.

pages.html:
Original distributed file: app/Docs/AgentGuide.md.

text
# Créer un CyTool avec une IA Ce document est le contrat de travail à fournir à une IA chargée de créer un Tool.Il s'applique à Codex, Claude, OpenCode ou tout autre assistant, sans dépendance au client. ## Résultat attendu Lire [StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md](StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md) : journalsélectionnable/copiable, pixels vidéo visibles, bibliothèque de dérivés, LoRA compatibleset sélection CPU/GPU réelle, enregistrés dans les configurations de génération. Pour les Tools de maillage (génération, remesh, PBR, UV, rig), lire[MeshViewer.md](MeshViewer.md) : utiliser `--desktop --mesh-viewer` et fournir leviewport interactif avec résultat automatique, caméra libre/orbitale et éclairage. Interface anglaise par defaut, francaise en option. Lire [Localization.md](Localization.md) :onglet Options, preferences persistantes, theme/taille du texte et licences de chaque composant.Lire [SharedInstallation.md](SharedInstallation.md) : cache local/partagé configurable,CUDA Toolkit enregistré et sélectionné explicitement, Python privé et installationguidée des composants absents, avec états d'accès structurés utilisables par une IA. Une application autonome avec interface **Dear ImGui obligatoire**, un vrai lanceurWindows `.exe`, un lanceur Linux adapté et une racine rangée `app/data/runtime`.Le manifeste et les sources résident dans `app/`. Les modèles et résultats sont dans`data/`. La CLI et le MCP complètent l'interface. Lire et appliquer intégralement[StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md) : installation guidée des modèles,autorisations/licences, mises à jour GitHub, restauration et contrôles de livraison.Ne pas créer CyToolsManager et ne pas ajouter une dépendance UI au Core. ## Informations à déterminer avant l'implémentation | Information | Exemple | Emplacement ||---|---|---|| Nom et ID stable | CyToolExample / cy.tool.example | name / id || Version métier | 0.1.0 | version || Opérations | echo, convert, inspect | operations || Entrées et contraintes | text requis, steps entre 1 et 100 | inputSchema || Sorties exactes | objet avec file et mimeType | outputSchema + outputs || Exécutable externe | python, ffmpeg, programme natif | runtimeRequirements || Plateformes | Windows x64 Supported ; macOS Unknown | platforms || Backends / modèles | moteur, versions, fichiers, licences | backends[].models[] || Budget par job | RAM, VRAM par device, disque, threads CPU | resourceRequirements / estimate || Parallélisme sûr | Sequential par défaut | concurrency || Effets et accès nécessaires | network, filesystemExternal | permissions || Répertoire de données | chemin dédié au Tool/service | --data-dir || Transport | CLI seule, service partagé, pont MCP | commandes de lancement | Si une valeur est inconnue, l'écrire comme telle. Ne pas inventer une consommationVRAM, une compatibilité GPU ou un modèle installé. Les booléens de capacité décriventle code livré, pas un objectif futur. Toutes les tailles sont en **octets**, les duréesen **secondes**, la progression entre **0 et 100**. ## Procédure reproductible 1. Installer le SDK depuis le dépôt local ou le wheel fourni ; Python >= 3.11.2. Exécuter `cytools new CHEMIN --name CyToolExample --id cy.tool.example --desktop`.3. Lire les fichiers générés et conserver le point d'entrée `run_cli(create_runtime)`.4. Remplacer l'opération echo par les opérations du Tool dans `CyTool.json`.5. Implémenter un handler par opération et les enregistrer dans `create_runtime`.6. Déclarer les ressources fixes ; ajouter un estimateur si elles dépendent des paramètres.7. Isoler un runtime lourd dans `ProcessWorker` ; définir son protocole de sortie JSON.8. Ajouter des tests du comportement réel, des entrées invalides, de l'annulation,   de l'échec métier, des sorties et de l'isolation de deux clients.9. Exécuter validation du manifest, tests du Tool, CLI describe/invoke et test MCP.10. Finaliser ImGui, le parcours d'installation des modèles et les mises à jour GitHub.11. Compiler/packager les lanceurs ; ranger la distribution et tester le lancement réel.12. Documenter installation, configuration, dépendances, modèles, preuves et limites. ## Contrat Python exact ```pythonfrom pathlib import Pathfrom cytools_core import Runtime, load_manifest, CyToolErrorfrom cytools_core.transports.cli import run_cli def create_runtime(data_dir, **options):    runtime = Runtime(load_manifest(Path(__file__).with_name('CyTool.json')),                      data_dir, **options)     def write_report(context, parameters):        context.cancellation.check()        path = context.path('outputs/report.txt')        path.write_text(parameters['text'], encoding='utf-8')        context.progress(100, currentStep='Written', currentStepIndex=1, stepCount=1)        return {'file': str(path), 'mimeType': 'text/plain'}     def estimate(parameters, backend, model):        # Remplacer cet exemple par une estimation conservatrice du vrai traitement.        return {'ramBytes': 1048576,                'diskBytes': len(parameters['text'].encode('utf-8'))}     runtime.register('write_report', write_report, estimate=estimate)    return runtime if __name__ == '__main__':    raise SystemExit(run_cli(create_runtime))``` Ce code exige une opération `write_report` dans le manifest. Ne pas créer de dialectede validation concurrent. Utiliser `x-cy-kind` et `x-cy-ui` pour les informations visuelles.Exemple complet dans [Parameters.md](Parameters.md). Le format file est une annotation,pas une permission automatique de lecture d'un fichier arbitraire. ## Backends et modèles Une opération sans backend utilise `supportedBackends: []` et n'a pas besoin de modèle.Si un seul backend est déclaré pour l'opération, il est sélectionné par défaut.Avec plusieurs backends, fournir backendId explicitement. modelId est facultatif mais,si fourni, doit appartenir au backend et être installé pour une exécution locale.L'estimateur reçoit `(parameters, backend_descriptor_or_None, model_descriptor_or_None)`.Les métadonnées d'un modèle ne constituent pas son implémentation : son installation,son chargement et son exécution appartiennent à l'adaptateur du Tool. Pour 10 Gio de VRAM : `{'vramBytes': {'auto': 10 * 1024**3}}` choisit un GPU admissible ;`{'vramBytes': {'0': 6 * 1024**3, '1': 6 * 1024**3}}` réserve deux GPU.Le backend doit effectivement savoir répartir le calcul. Ne pas mettre `simulation`dans un vrai Tool : ce device appartient aux tests. ## Partage entre plusieurs clients Pour partager une file et un modèle, démarrer **un service** et connecter les clientsavec des jetons distincts. Voir [MultiClient.md](MultiClient.md). Plusieurs processusMCP autonomes lancés dans des dossiers différents ont des runtimes différents.Ne pas prétendre qu'ils partagent automatiquement leur VRAM ou leurs modèles. ## Définition de terminé Appliquer aussi tous les critères de [StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md).La génération d'un squelette ou une commande CLI réussie ne suffit pas. L'interface Dear ImGui doit respecter [Localization.md](Localization.md) : anglaispar défaut, français sélectionnable et onglet Options avec préférences et licences.Appliquer [GenerationConfigurations.md](GenerationConfigurations.md) : sauvegarde etchargement du formulaire, autosave optionnelle des paramètres soumis, JSON versionnéréutilisable par une IA et exclusion des secrets. Vérifier un aller-retour réel duformulaire et un rejeu via le runtime. Le chargement ne démarre jamais la génération. - `cytools validate CyTool.json` réussit.- La CLI décrit toutes les opérations implémentées et exécute un cas réel.- Les sorties valident outputSchema ; les chemins créés restent dans le workspace.- Un client B ne lit ni n'annule un job privé du client A.- L'annulation libère réellement le worker avant les réservations.- Un paramètre incorrect et une dépendance absente donnent un code d'erreur utile.- Le catalogue MCP est dérivé du manifest et l'appel crée un job consultable.- README donne des commandes testées et les variables d'environnement exactes.- Les plateformes testées sont distinguées des plateformes simplement déclarées. Pour un SDK natif C++/C#, reproduire le protocole et les mêmes fixtures de conformité.Une première intégration peut déjà utiliser le service HTTP ou un worker JSON stdin/stdout.Ne pas réécrire le scheduler dans chaque Tool.  Lire [FullOperationAccess.md](FullOperationAccess.md) : inventaire des capacités natives, parité complète des options métier entre IA et standalone, contrats de sorties composables et preuves de validation. FinishTask removes imported copies and generated workspaces after workers stop; export wanted results first. Standalone sessions explicitly use temporary=False.

Il s'applique à Codex, Claude, OpenCode ou tout autre assistant, sans dépendance au client. ## Résultat attendu Lire [StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md](StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md) : journal sélectionnable/copiable, pixels vidéo visibles, bibliothèque de dérivés, LoRA compatibles et sélection CPU/GPU réelle, enregistrés dans les configurations de génération. Pour les Tools de maillage (génération, remesh, PBR, UV, rig), lire [MeshViewer.md](MeshViewer.md) : utiliser `--desktop --mesh-viewer` et fournir le viewport interactif avec résultat automatique, caméra libre/orbitale et éclairage. Interface anglaise par defaut, francaise en option. Lire [Localization.md](Localization.md) : onglet Options, preferences persistantes, theme/taille du texte et licences de chaque composant. Lire [SharedInstallation.md](SharedInstallation.md) : cache local/partagé configurable, CUDA Toolkit enregistré et sélectionné explicitement, Python privé et installation guidée des composants absents, avec états d'accès structurés utilisables par une IA. Une application autonome avec interface **Dear ImGui obligatoire**, un vrai lanceur Windows `.exe`, un lanceur Linux adapté et une racine rangée `app/data/runtime`. Le manifeste et les sources résident dans `app/`. Les modèles et résultats sont dans `data/`. La CLI et le MCP complètent l'interface. Lire et appliquer intégralement [StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md) : installation guidée des modèles, autorisations/licences, mises à jour GitHub, restauration et contrôles de livraison. Ne pas créer CyToolsManager et ne pas ajouter une dépendance UI au Core. ## Informations à déterminer avant l'implémentation | Information | Exemple | Emplacement | |---|---|---| | Nom et ID stable | CyToolExample / cy.tool.example | name / id | | Version métier | 0.1.0 | version | | Opérations | echo, convert, inspect | operations | | Entrées et contraintes | text requis, steps entre 1 et 100 | inputSchema | | Sorties exactes | objet avec file et mimeType | outputSchema + outputs | | Exécutable externe | python, ffmpeg, programme natif | runtimeRequirements | | Plateformes | Windows x64 Supported ; macOS Unknown | platforms | | Backends / modèles | moteur, versions, fichiers, licences | backends[].models[] | | Budget par job | RAM, VRAM par device, disque, threads CPU | resourceRequirements / estimate | | Parallélisme sûr | Sequential par défaut | concurrency | | Effets et accès nécessaires | network, filesystemExternal | permissions | | Répertoire de données | chemin dédié au Tool/service | --data-dir | | Transport | CLI seule, service partagé, pont MCP | commandes de lancement | Si une valeur est inconnue, l'écrire comme telle. Ne pas inventer une consommation VRAM, une compatibilité GPU ou un modèle installé. Les booléens de capacité décrivent le code livré, pas un objectif futur. Toutes les tailles sont en **octets**, les durées en **secondes**, la progression entre **0 et 100**. ## Procédure reproductible 1. Installer le SDK depuis le dépôt local ou le wheel fourni ; Python >= 3.11. 2. Exécuter `cytools new CHEMIN --name CyToolExample --id cy.tool.example --desktop`. 3. Lire les fichiers générés et conserver le point d'entrée `run_cli(create_runtime)`. 4. Remplacer l'opération echo par les opérations du Tool dans `CyTool.json`. 5. Implémenter un handler par opération et les enregistrer dans `create_runtime`. 6. Déclarer les ressources fixes ; ajouter un estimateur si elles dépendent des paramètres. 7. Isoler un runtime lourd dans `ProcessWorker` ; définir son protocole de sortie JSON. 8. Ajouter des tests du comportement réel, des entrées invalides, de l'annulation, de l'échec métier, des sorties et de l'isolation de deux clients. 9. Exécuter validation du manifest, tests du Tool, CLI describe/invoke et test MCP. 10. Finaliser ImGui, le parcours d'installation des modèles et les mises à jour GitHub. 11. Compiler/packager les lanceurs ; ranger la distribution et tester le lancement réel. 12. Documenter installation, configuration, dépendances, modèles, preuves et limites. ## Contrat Python exact ```python from pathlib import Path from cytools_core import Runtime, load_manifest, CyToolError from cytools_core.transports.cli import run_cli def create_runtime(data_dir, **options): runtime = Runtime(load_manifest(Path(__file__).with_name('CyTool.json')), data_dir, **options) def write_report(context, parameters): context.cancellation.check() path = context.path('outputs/report.txt') path.write_text(parameters['text'], encoding='utf-8') context.progress(100, currentStep='Written', currentStepIndex=1, stepCount=1) return {'file': str(path), 'mimeType': 'text/plain'} def estimate(parameters, backend, model): # Remplacer cet exemple par une estimation conservatrice du vrai traitement. return {'ramBytes': 1048576, 'diskBytes': len(parameters['text'].encode('utf-8'))} runtime.register('write_report', write_report, estimate=estimate) return runtime if __name__ == '__main__': raise SystemExit(run_cli(create_runtime)) ``` Ce code exige une opération `write_report` dans le manifest. Son `inputSchema` doit contenir `text` string requis ; son `outputSchema` doit contenir `file` et `mimeType` string requis. Le handler reçoit une copie validée des paramètres, avec les valeurs par défaut appliquées. Il retourne un objet JSON conforme à outputSchema. Un retour invalide fait échouer le job avec `InvalidOutput`. Pour un échec attendu, lever `CyToolError('MissingDependency', 'Message utile', recoverable=True)`. Ne pas appeler `runtime.start()` dans la factory : le lanceur et les tests gèrent le cycle de vie. Ne pas imprimer sur stdout depuis les handlers ; utiliser `context.log(message, level='Info')`. Le Core ne peut pas interrompre de force un thread Python ; un programme non coopératif doit être isolé dans un worker. ## Paramètres conditionnels et UI Employer JSON Schema 2020-12 : type, properties, required, default, enum, minimum, maximum, multipleOf, items, $defs/$ref locaux et if/then/else. Ne pas créer de dialecte de validation concurrent. Utiliser `x-cy-kind` et `x-cy-ui` pour les informations visuelles. Exemple complet dans [Parameters.md](Parameters.md). Le format file est une annotation, pas une permission automatique de lecture d'un fichier arbitraire. ## Backends et modèles Une opération sans backend utilise `supportedBackends: []` et n'a pas besoin de modèle. Si un seul backend est déclaré pour l'opération, il est sélectionné par défaut. L'estimateur reçoit `(parameters, backend_descriptor_or_None, model_descriptor_or_None)`. Les métadonnées d'un modèle ne constituent pas son implémentation : son installation, son chargement et son exécution appartiennent à l'adaptateur du Tool. Pour 10 Gio de VRAM : `{'vramBytes': {'auto': 10 * 1024**3}}` choisit un GPU admissible ; `{'vramBytes': {'0': 6 * 1024**3, '1': 6 * 1024**3}}` réserve deux GPU. Le backend doit effectivement savoir répartir le calcul. Ne pas mettre `simulation` dans un vrai Tool : ce device appartient aux tests. ## Partage entre plusieurs clients Pour partager une file et un modèle, démarrer **un service** et connecter les clients avec des jetons distincts. Voir [MultiClient.md](MultiClient.md). Plusieurs processus MCP autonomes lancés dans des dossiers différents ont des runtimes différents. Ne pas prétendre qu'ils partagent automatiquement leur VRAM ou leurs modèles. ## Définition de terminé Appliquer aussi tous les critères de [StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md). La génération d'un squelette ou une commande CLI réussie ne suffit pas. L'interface Dear ImGui doit respecter [Localization.md](Localization.md) : anglais par défaut, français sélectionnable et onglet Options avec préférences et licences. # Créer un CyTool avec une IA

Ce document est le contrat de travail à fournir à une IA chargée de créer un Tool.
Il s'applique à Codex, Claude, OpenCode ou tout autre assistant, sans dépendance au client.

## Résultat attendu

Lire [StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md](StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md) : journal
sélectionnable/copiable, pixels vidéo visibles, bibliothèque de dérivés, LoRA compatibles
et sélection CPU/GPU réelle, enregistrés dans les configurations de génération.

Pour les Tools de maillage (génération, remesh, PBR, UV, rig), lire
[MeshViewer.md](MeshViewer.md) : utiliser `--desktop --mesh-viewer` et fournir le
viewport interactif avec résultat automatique, caméra libre/orbitale et éclairage.

Interface anglaise par defaut, francaise en option. Lire [Localization.md](Localization.md) :
onglet Options, preferences persistantes, theme/taille du texte et licences de chaque composant.
Lire [SharedInstallation.md](SharedInstallation.md) : cache local/partagé configurable,
CUDA Toolkit enregistré et sélectionné explicitement, Python privé et installation
guidée des composants absents, avec états d'accès structurés utilisables par une IA.

Une application autonome avec interface **Dear ImGui obligatoire**, un vrai lanceur
Windows `.exe`, un lanceur Linux adapté et une racine rangée `app/data/runtime`.
Le manifeste et les sources résident dans `app/`. Les modèles et résultats sont dans
`data/`. La CLI et le MCP complètent l'interface. Lire et appliquer intégralement
[StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md) : installation guidée des modèles,
autorisations/licences, mises à jour GitHub, restauration et contrôles de livraison.
Ne pas créer CyToolsManager et ne pas ajouter une dépendance UI au Core.

## Informations à déterminer avant l'implémentation

| Information | Exemple | Emplacement |
|---|---|---|
| Nom et ID stable | CyToolExample / cy.tool.example | name / id |
| Version métier | 0.1.0 | version |
| Opérations | echo, convert, inspect | operations |
| Entrées et contraintes | text requis, steps entre 1 et 100 | inputSchema |
| Sorties exactes | objet avec file et mimeType | outputSchema + outputs |
| Exécutable externe | python, ffmpeg, programme natif | runtimeRequirements |
| Plateformes | Windows x64 Supported ; macOS Unknown | platforms |
| Backends / modèles | moteur, versions, fichiers, licences | backends[].models[] |
| Budget par job | RAM, VRAM par device, disque, threads CPU | resourceRequirements / estimate |
| Parallélisme sûr | Sequential par défaut | concurrency |
| Effets et accès nécessaires | network, filesystemExternal | permissions |
| Répertoire de données | chemin dédié au Tool/service | --data-dir |
| Transport | CLI seule, service partagé, pont MCP | commandes de lancement |

Si une valeur est inconnue, l'écrire comme telle. Ne pas inventer une consommation
VRAM, une compatibilité GPU ou un modèle installé. Les booléens de capacité décrivent
le code livré, pas un objectif futur. Toutes les tailles sont en **octets**, les durées
en **secondes**, la progression entre **0 et 100**.

## Procédure reproductible

1. Installer le SDK depuis le dépôt local ou le wheel fourni ; Python >= 3.11.
2. Exécuter `cytools new CHEMIN --name CyToolExample --id cy.tool.example --desktop`.
3. Lire les fichiers générés et conserver le point d'entrée `run_cli(create_runtime)`.
4. Remplacer l'opération echo par les opérations du Tool dans `CyTool.json`.
5. Implémenter un handler par opération et les enregistrer dans `create_runtime`.
6. Déclarer les ressources fixes ; ajouter un estimateur si elles dépendent des paramètres.
7. Isoler un runtime lourd dans `ProcessWorker` ; définir son protocole de sortie JSON.
8. Ajouter des tests du comportement réel, des entrées invalides, de l'annulation,
   de l'échec métier, des sorties et de l'isolation de deux clients.
9. Exécuter validation du manifest, tests du Tool, CLI describe/invoke et test MCP.
10. Finaliser ImGui, le parcours d'installation des modèles et les mises à jour GitHub.
11. Compiler/packager les lanceurs ; ranger la distribution et tester le lancement réel.
12. Documenter installation, configuration, dépendances, modèles, preuves et limites.

## Contrat Python exact

```python
from pathlib import Path
from cytools_core import Runtime, load_manifest, CyToolError
from cytools_core.transports.cli import run_cli

def create_runtime(data_dir, **options):
    runtime = Runtime(load_manifest(Path(__file__).with_name('CyTool.json')),
                      data_dir, **options)

    def write_report(context, parameters):
        context.cancellation.check()
        path = context.path('outputs/report.txt')
        path.write_text(parameters['text'], encoding='utf-8')
        context.progress(100, currentStep='Written', currentStepIndex=1, stepCount=1)
        return {'file': str(path), 'mimeType': 'text/plain'}

    def estimate(parameters, backend, model):
        # Remplacer cet exemple par une estimation conservatrice du vrai traitement.
        return {'ramBytes': 1048576,
                'diskBytes': len(parameters['text'].encode('utf-8'))}

    runtime.register('write_report', write_report, estimate=estimate)
    return runtime

if __name__ == '__main__':
    raise SystemExit(run_cli(create_runtime))
```

Ce code exige une opération `write_report` dans le manifest. Son `inputSchema`
doit contenir `text` string requis ; son `outputSchema` doit contenir `file` et
`mimeType` string requis. Déclarer `supportsProgress: true`, `canCancel: true`,
`canRunAsync: true`. `file` peut porter `x-cy-kind: File` pour une future UI.

Le handler reçoit une copie validée des paramètres, avec les valeurs par défaut
appliquées. Il retourne un objet JSON conforme à outputSchema. Un retour invalide
fait échouer le job avec `InvalidOutput`. Pour un échec attendu, lever
`CyToolError('MissingDependency', 'Message utile', recoverable=True)`.

Ne pas appeler `runtime.start()` dans la factory : le lanceur et les tests gèrent
le cycle de vie. Ne pas imprimer sur stdout depuis les handlers ; utiliser
`context.log(message, level='Info')`. Les opérations natives longues doivent appeler
`context.cancellation.check()` régulièrement. Le Core ne peut pas interrompre de force
un thread Python ; un programme non coopératif doit être isolé dans un worker.

## Paramètres conditionnels et UI

Employer JSON Schema 2020-12 : type, properties, required, default, enum, minimum,
maximum, multipleOf, items, $defs/$ref locaux et if/then/else. Ne pas créer de dialecte
de validation concurrent. Utiliser `x-cy-kind` et `x-cy-ui` pour les informations visuelles.
Exemple complet dans [Parameters.md](Parameters.md). Le format file est une annotation,
pas une permission automatique de lecture d'un fichier arbitraire.

## Backends et modèles

Une opération sans backend utilise `supportedBackends: []` et n'a pas besoin de modèle.
Si un seul backend est déclaré pour l'opération, il est sélectionné par défaut.
Avec plusieurs backends, fournir backendId explicitement. modelId est facultatif mais,
si fourni, doit appartenir au backend et être installé pour une exécution locale.
L'estimateur reçoit `(parameters, backend_descriptor_or_None, model_descriptor_or_None)`.
Les métadonnées d'un modèle ne constituent pas son implémentation : son installation,
son chargement et son exécution appartiennent à l'adaptateur du Tool.

Pour 10 Gio de VRAM : `{'vramBytes': {'auto': 10 * 1024**3}}` choisit un GPU admissible ;
`{'vramBytes': {'0': 6 * 1024**3, '1': 6 * 1024**3}}` réserve deux GPU.
Le backend doit effectivement savoir répartir le calcul. Ne pas mettre `simulation`
dans un vrai Tool : ce device appartient aux tests.

## Partage entre plusieurs clients

Pour partager une file et un modèle, démarrer **un service** et connecter les clients
avec des jetons distincts. Voir [MultiClient.md](MultiClient.md). Plusieurs processus
MCP autonomes lancés dans des dossiers différents ont des runtimes différents.
Ne pas prétendre qu'ils partagent automatiquement leur VRAM ou leurs modèles.

## Définition de terminé

Appliquer aussi tous les critères de [StandaloneDelivery.md](StandaloneDelivery.md).
La génération d'un squelette ou une commande CLI réussie ne suffit pas.

L'interface Dear ImGui doit respecter [Localization.md](Localization.md) : anglais
par défaut, français sélectionnable et onglet Options avec préférences et licences.
Appliquer [GenerationConfigurations.md](GenerationConfigurations.md) : sauvegarde et
chargement du formulaire, autosave optionnelle des paramètres soumis, JSON versionné
réutilisable par une IA et exclusion des secrets. Vérifier un aller-retour réel du
formulaire et un rejeu via le runtime. Le chargement ne démarre jamais la génération.

- `cytools validate CyTool.json` réussit.
- La CLI décrit toutes les opérations implémentées et exécute un cas réel.
- Les sorties valident outputSchema ; les chemins créés restent dans le workspace.
- Un client B ne lit ni n'annule un job privé du client A.
- L'annulation libère réellement le worker avant les réservations.
- Un paramètre incorrect et une dépendance absente donnent un code d'erreur utile.
- Le catalogue MCP est dérivé du manifest et l'appel crée un job consultable.
- README donne des commandes testées et les variables d'environnement exactes.
- Les plateformes testées sont distinguées des plateformes simplement déclarées.

Pour un SDK natif C++/C#, reproduire le protocole et les mêmes fixtures de conformité.
Une première intégration peut déjà utiliser le service HTTP ou un worker JSON stdin/stdout.
Ne pas réécrire le scheduler dans chaque Tool.


Lire [FullOperationAccess.md](FullOperationAccess.md) : inventaire des capacités natives, parité complète des options métier entre IA et standalone, contrats de sorties composables et preuves de validation. Un formulaire simplifié ne limite pas le contrat du Tool.

Lire Docs/AutomaticInputs.md (AutomaticInputs.md depuis Docs) : chemins absolus acceptés pour les entrées locales, copie automatique privée par job, aucune copie manuelle exigée de l’IA.


## Task-owned files (SDK 0.9.0)

Read Docs/TaskFiles.md (TaskFiles.md from this Docs directory). Configure input roots and all file fields for automatic imports; AI sessions are temporary by default. FinishTask removes imported copies and generated workspaces after workers stop; export wanted results first. Standalone sessions explicitly use temporary=False.

# Prompt prêt à fournir à une IA

## Prompt court pour un nouveau Tool

```text
Crée CyTools_<NOM> dans un nouveau sous-dossier <TOOLS_ROOT>/CyTools_<NOM>.
Fonction : <DESCRIPTION COURTE>.
Suis toutes les instructions de <SDK_ROOT>\Docs\AgentPrompt.md,
ainsi que les documents qu'il référence. Ne modifie pas les autres Tools.
```

## Instructions complètes de création

Remplacer les champs entre chevrons. Les documents cités sont obligatoires.

```text
Crée une application CyTools autonome nommée <NOM>, ID <ID>, dans <TOOLS_ROOT>/<NOM>.
Fonction attendue : <DESCRIPTION DU MODÈLE/OUTIL, ENTRÉES, SORTIES ET OPTIONS>.
Sources officielles : <URL DU MOTEUR, PAGE DU MODÈLE, DÉPÔT GITHUB DU TOOL SI DISPONIBLE>.

SDK local : <SDK_ROOT>. Lis d’abord AGENTS.md, README.md,
Docs/AgentGuide.md, Docs/StandaloneDelivery.md, Docs/Architecture.md et
Docs/ImplementationStatus.md. Utilise cytools new --desktop ; ne copie jamais le runtime.

Livre une racine épurée : <NOM>.exe, lanceur Linux, LISEZ-MOI.md, app/, data/, runtime/.
Range code, manifeste, tests et scripts dans app ; modèles, entrées, jobs, réglages et
logs dans data ; environnements privés, sources de moteurs, téléchargements et versions
dans runtime. Nettoie les artefacts de développement avant livraison sans supprimer de données.

L’exécutable Windows doit ouvrir directement une vraie interface Dear ImGui.
L'interface est en anglais par defaut et entierement disponible en francais.
Applique Docs/Localization.md : onglet Options avec langue persistante, theme,
taille du texte et licences du Tool, du moteur, des modeles et des dependances,
avec liens officiels. Ne suppose aucun droit pour une licence non renseignee.
Ajoute Save/Load configuration et Autosave on generation dans Options, en appliquant
Docs/GenerationConfigurations.md : JSON versionne, parametres exacts reutilisables
par une IA, aucun secret, chargement sans execution automatique.
Applique Docs/SharedInstallation.md : cache local/partagé configurable, Python privé,
CUDA Toolkit partagé explicitement sélectionné et version vérifiée, états structurés
pour l'IA en cas de connexion/licence nécessaire. Ne déplace aucun modèle existant.
Distribue sans poids, caches et gros environnements ; guide leur installation au premier lancement.
Toutes les capacités annoncées doivent être utilisables dans cette interface : sélection
entrée/modèle/backend, réglages usuels et avancés, génération, progression réelle,
annulation, erreurs, diagnostic et accès/aperçu des résultats. Pas de JSON à éditer pour
l’usage normal. CLI et MCP utilisent le même runtime et les mêmes schémas.
Pour tout Tool qui produit/modifie un mesh, applique Docs/MeshViewer.md et utilise
--desktop --mesh-viewer : vrai viewport 3D, ouverture automatique du résultat, navigation
souris/clavier en orbite et libre, inspection rapprochée, scènes, studio trois points
et soleil, matériaux PBR. Une image fixe ou un lanceur externe ne suffit pas.

Ajoute un écran d’installation des modèles : état, taille, source, licence, boutons
Télécharger/Reprendre/Réparer/Annuler. Si autorisation requise, fournir instructions et
liens officiels, puis une connexion locale sécurisée. L’utilisateur accepte lui-même la
licence. Aucun jeton dans argv, paramètres de jobs, manifeste ou logs. Vérifie les fichiers
et prépare les modèles auxiliaires ; n’annonce pas un modèle installé avant contrôle.

Ajoute les mises à jour GitHub de l’application et du moteur en les distinguant des poids.
Source configurée, vérification et téléchargement automatiques optionnels, staging,
contrôles de version/hash/ABI/archives, activation hors génération, sauvegarde et retour
arrière. Préserve data. Si le dépôt du Tool n’existe pas, rends-le configurable et indique
cette limite ; n’invente ni URL, ni release, ni test réussi.

Conserve jobs, identités authentifiées, workspaces, réservations et annulation du SDK.
Isole le modèle dans un worker ; libère les ressources seulement après son arrêt réel.
Aucune dépendance ImGui ou IA dans le Core. Crée les environnements à leur chemin final.

Teste le lanceur et les écrans ImGui, un traitement réel et ses sorties, l’installation,
les erreurs d’accès, l’annulation, l’isolation, le MCP, les mises à jour et leur rollback.
Distingue Windows/Linux exécutés, tests avec fixtures et fonctions encore non vérifiées.
Un scaffold CLI/MCP n’est pas une livraison terminée. Livre le dossier rangé, un guide
court et les preuves dans data/reports. Décris honnêtement les prérequis du runtime.
```
# Exigences complémentaires obligatoires

Appliquer `Docs/StandaloneDiagnosticsAndModels.md` : journal intégré sélectionnable
et copiable, résolution vidéo prévue/réelle visible, ajout de modèles locaux compatibles,
LoRA avec intensités lorsque le moteur sait les charger, et sélection CPU/GPU/Auto
avec ressources et exécution cohérentes. Conserver ces sélections dans Save/Load/Autosave.


Lire [FullOperationAccess.md](FullOperationAccess.md) : inventaire des capacités natives, parité complète des options métier entre IA et standalone, contrats de sorties composables et preuves de validation. Un formulaire simplifié ne limite pas le contrat du Tool.
